body.translated_text: <s>Īśvarasiddhi</s> (Proof of God's Existence)
Accompanied by the commentary named <s>Siddhāñjana</s>.
(Sūtra) There, the universe operates under the control of a certain single one;
to establish this, we first state the prior objection (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>). || 1 ||

children.text: tatra mīmāṃsakāḥ prāhuḥ - nāyaṃ sarvārthadarśanaśaktisampannaḥ puruṣo 'bhyupagamamarhati, atipatitasakalasādhakapramāṇasambhāvanābhūmitvātsphuṭavividhabādhakatvācca / tathāhi - asya papratyakṣamanyadvā sādhakaṃ bhavet ? pratyakṣamapi laukikaṃ yaugikaṃ vā ?
children.translated_text: There the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> say: This person endowed with the power of perceiving all objects does not deserve to be accepted, because the scope for all proving means of knowledge has been exceeded, and because of clear and diverse refutations. For instance: Would perception or something else be the proof for this? And is the perception ordinary or yogic?

body.translated_text: (Commentary) Having meditated upon the feet of <s>Śrīpati</s> and bowing to the pair of lotus-feet of the teacher,
I compose an elegant exposition of the <s>Īśvarasiddhi</s> for the purpose of easy understanding. || 1 ||
The Lord, established by the end of the Vedas (<s>Vedānta</s>), is considered by thinkers of sound reasoning constantly;

body.text: bhaktyā dhyānābhyāsāt prakaṭaḥ prajñāṃ tanotu me śubhrām // 2 //
body.translated_text: made manifest through <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) and the practice of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), may He extend to me pure wisdom. || 2 ||

children.text: atha khalu tatrabhavān paramācāryaḥ śrīmadbhagavadyāmunamunirātmacintāṃ vidhāyātmasiddhau paramātmacintāṃ vidadhadīśvarasiddhāvīśvarasādhakapramāṇavyavasthāpanāyopakramamāṇaḥ pratijānīte tatre ti / samastamaṃ cetanācatanātmakaṃ jagat ekasya - sarveśvarasya vaśe - icchāyāṃ saṅkalpalakṣaṇāyāṃ pravartateprakarṣeṇa vartate - asaṅkīrṇasvarūpasvabhāvavyavasthamāste, pravartate ca sve sve karmaṇi yathāyathamiti kṛtsnasya sarveśvarasaṅkalpādhīnasvarūpasthitipravṛttikatvaṃ sādhayituṃ - pramāṇato vyavasthāpayituṃ, prathamataḥ pūrvapakṣaṃ varṇayāma iti kārikārthaḥ / atra tatreti prakāntaparāmarśakatacchabdanirdeśādetatpūrvatanaḥ kaścaneśvarasiddhagranthabhāgaḥ syāt , yo bahoḥ kālātpūrvamevavilupta ityabhyūhyate 1
children.translated_text: Now then, the revered supreme teacher, the glorious divine sage <s>Yāmuna</s>, having set forth the investigation of the self in the <s>Ātmasiddhi</s>, engaging in the investigation of the Supreme Self in the <s>Īśvarasiddhi</s>, beginning for the purpose of establishing the means of proof for God, states 'there' as follows: The entire universe consisting of the conscious and unconscious, under the control of one—the Lord of all—operates according to His will characterized by volition, functions supremely, remains established with unmixed essential nature and character, and operates in its respective activities appropriately. Thus, to prove that the essential nature, existence, and activity of everything depends on the will of the Lord of all—to establish this by means of proof—we first describe the prior objection. This is the meaning of the verse. Here, the word 'tatra' with its demonstrative reference to something prior suggests that there may have been an earlier portion of the <s>Īśvarasiddhi</s> text, which is conjectured to have been lost long ago. || 1 ||

body.translated_text: Ordinary [perception], whose objects are fixed and limited, is not in this case
a means of proof, because of the unestablishedness of all objects and their cognition etc. by that [ordinary perception]. || 2 ||

children.text:
sarvārthadarśanaśaktiśālinamavagamayatā hi deśakālasvabhāvaviprakarṣavyavadhānajuṣaḥ sarva evārthāstaddarśanaṃ śaktiśca gocarayitavyāni / na ca vidyamānendriyasannikarṣayogyakatipayaviṣayanipatavṛtterlaukikapratyakṣasya niravadhirayaṃ mahimā saṃbhāvanābhūmiriti kathamiva tadiha sādhanamiti manyemahi/
'nāyam' iti / sarvārthasākṣātkakārasarvakāryopajananaśakti sampannaścetanaviśeṣa īśvaraśabditaḥ sādhakābhāvādbādhakabalācca nāṅgīkartuṃ yogya ityarthaḥ / ' atipatite ' ti / atipatitā - apakrāntā sakalasādhakapramāṇasambhāvanā yasyāḥ evambhūtā bhūmirviṣayaḥ, tattvāt - vyapetasakalasādhakapramāṇasambhāvanātmakaviṣayatvādityarthaḥ / atra iti 'atipatitasakalasādhakapramāṇasaṃbhāvanābhūmitvatvā' diti 'atipatitasakala sādhakapramāṇasaṃbhāvanābhūmitvatvā'diti vā pāṭhaḥ sambhāvyate / 'sphuṭe' ti / sphuṭāni - prasiddhāni vividhāni bādhakāni yasyaivambhūtatvāccetyarthaḥ / upakṣiptayorīśvare sādhakābhāvabādhakabhāvayoḥ sādhakābhāvaṃ tāvadādau samarthayitumupakramate 'tathāhi'tyādinā / anyat - anumānādi /
children.translated_text: The commentator explains the inability of ordinary perception to prove God, stating: For one who would make known [a being] endowed with the power of perceiving all objects must bring within the scope [of perception] all objects—which span distances of place, time, and nature and are separated by obstructions—along with the perception of them and the power itself. But ordinary perception, which operates only upon a few objects that are accessible through present sense-object contact, cannot possibly have this unlimited scope—how then could it be a means of proof here? This is what we maintain. 'This [person]' means the particular conscious being designated by the word <s>Īśvara</s> (God), endowed with the power of directly perceiving all objects and generating all effects, is not fit to be acknowledged due to the absence of proof and the force of refutation. 'Exceeded' means the scope—whose subject matter is devoid of the possibility of all proving means of knowledge—has been exceeded. The reading may be either 'atipatitasakalasādhakapramāṇasaṃbhāvanābhūmitvāt' or an alternative form. 'Clear' means because of being such that the refutations are manifest and diverse. Having introduced both the absence of proof and the presence of refutation regarding God, the author begins to substantiate the absence of proof first with 'For instance.' 'Other' means inference and the like.

body.text: laukikasyendriyārthasannikarṣajasya pratyakṣasyeśvarāsādhakatāmupapādayati 'vyavasthite'ti / hetugarbhamidaṃ viśeṣaṇam / laukikapratyakṣasya viṣayā yataḥ parimitā vyavasthitāśca, ata ityarthaḥ / iha - īśvare viṣaye / sādhanaṃsādhakam / pramāṇamiti yāvat / tena - laukikapratyakṣeṇa / asiddhitaḥ -aprakāśataḥ / ayaṃ bhāvaḥ - cākṣuṣasya tāvat pratyakṣasya rūparūpirūpaikārthasamavetasaṅkhyādaya eva viṣayāḥ, na tu rasādaya iti parimitatā / udbhūtānabhibhūtameva rūpaṃ mahattvaikādhikaraṇaṃ grāhyaṃ na tu paramāṇvādigatamiti tatrāpi vyavasthitatā / evaṃ rāsanādiṣvapi bodhyam / evaṃbhūtasya caindriyikapratyakṣasya sarvārthāderaprakāśakatvānneśvare pramāṇatvaṃ sambhavati / sarvārthadarśanakaraṇasāmarthyaviśiṣṭo hyabhimataḥ saḥ / sarvārthasya tadgrahaṇasya tacchakteśca grahaṇamantarā ca na tasya grahaṇaṃ ghaṭate / sarvārtheṣvayogyānāmapi praviṣṭatvācchakteścātīndriyatvāt , jñānasya bahirindriyāgrāhyatvādvāhyārthānāṃ ca kevalena manasāgrahānnendriyeṇa kenāpi sarvārthādergrahaṇam / tadgrahaṇamantarā ca na viśiṣṭeśvaragrahaṇam /
body.translated_text: The commentator demonstrates the inability of sensory perception—born from sense-object contact—to prove God with 'fixed.' This qualifying expression contains the reason. Since the objects of ordinary perception are limited and fixed, therefore—this is the meaning. 'Here' means in the subject matter of God. 'Means of proof' means a valid means of knowledge. 'By that' means by ordinary perception. 'Unestablishedness' means non-manifestation. The purport is this: Visual perception, for instance, has only form and entities co-present with form—such as number—as its objects, not taste and the like; thus it is limited. And even regarding form, only manifest, unobscured form that is co-located with magnitude is graspable, not that belonging to atoms and the like; thus there is fixedness even there. The same should be understood for the sense of taste and others. Such sensory perception, being unable to manifest all objects, cannot be a means of knowledge regarding God. For He is intended as one endowed with the capacity to perceive all objects. And without grasping all objects, the perception of them, and the power thereof, the grasp of Him is not possible. Since all objects include those that are unfit for any sense organ, and the power is supersensible, and cognition is not graspable by external senses, and external objects cannot be grasped by mind alone—by what sense organ could all objects and the like be grasped? And without grasping them, there is no grasping of the qualified God,

body.text: 'nāgṛhītaviśeṣaṇe' ti nyāyāt / tadaindriyikalaukikapratyakṣaṃ neśvare pramāṇaṃ bhavitumarhatīti // 2 //
body.translated_text: according to the principle that '[something cannot be cognized] without its qualifier being cognized.' Therefore, sensory ordinary perception cannot be a means of valid knowledge regarding God. || 2 ||

children.translated_text: Nor is yogic perception a proof for this, because—

body.translated_text: If it is a perception, then it too is limited to a single existent object;
cognition directed at past objects and the like is never perception, like intuition (<s>pratibhā</s>) and such. || 3 ||

body.text: tat khalu yogivijñānamaindriyikaṃ na vā ? aindriyikamapi bahirindriyasambhavamāntarakaraṇajanitaṃ vā ? bahirindriyāṇi tāvatsamadhigatanijaviṣayasannikarṣasahakārīṇi tadgocarajñānajananānīti jagati viditam / ato na rasanādibhirajātātivṛttavyavahitādi sakalaviṣayavedanaprasaṅgaḥ / na cāvidyamānairajātādibhiḥ saṃbhavati sannikarṣaḥ ; tasya dvyāśrayatvādāśrayābhāve tadasambhavāt / ato 'pekṣitor'thasannikarṣaḥ / sahakārivirahe kathamindriyāṇyatītādiviṣayasākṣātkārāya kalperan? / bhavati ca - yat yatsahakāri yatkāryajananam , tattadabhāve na tajjanayati ; yathā kṣitisalilasahakāri aṅkarakāryajananabījaṃ kṣityādyabhāve 'ṅkaram / arthasannikarṣasahakārīṇi bahirindriyāṇi jñānajananānīti tānyapi nātīte 'nāgate vār'the jñānaṃ janayantīti na tadupajanitaṃ pratyakṣaṃ yathoktaviṣayaniyamamatikrāmati / nāpyāntarakaraṇasambhavam , āntaragocara eva sukhādau svāntasvātatryāt / bāhyaviṣayamitiṣu ca manaso niraṅkuśakaraṇatāṅgīkāre hi kṛtaṃ cakṣurādibhiḥ / ataśca na kaścidandho badhiro vā bhavet / bhavati cātra - vimatipadaṃ mano bahirindriyanirapekṣaṃ na bāhyapratyakṣagocare pravartate, tatra tattantravṛttitvāt / yadyatra yattantravṛtti na tattannirapekṣaṃ tatra pravartate, yathā'lokāpekṣapravṛtti cakṣuḥ svagocare 'ndhatamasa iti / na ca siddhauṣadhamatpratapaḥsamādhimahimasamāsāditātiśayānīndriyāṇi kadācidapajahati samādhigataviṣayaniyamamiti sambhavati ; sāṃsiddhikasāmarthyāvirbhāvaikaphalatvātteṣām , sāmarthyasya ca pratiniyamāt / na khalu suprayuktabheṣajaśatavihitasaṃskāramapi śrotraṃ rūparasavibhāgāvagamāya kalpate / bhavati ca - vivādādhyāsitabāhyabhyantarakaraṇapāṭavātiśayo 'nullaṅghitasīmā, aindriyikaprakarṣatvāt , dṛśyamānatatprakarṣavat ityaindriyikaṃ jñānaṃ nātītādi gocarayati /
body.translated_text: Now, is that yogic cognition produced by the senses or not? If sensory, is it produced by external senses or generated by the internal organ? As for external senses, it is well known in the world that they generate cognition of their respective objects when assisted by contact with their established specific objects. Therefore, there is no possibility that the tongue and other senses could cognize all objects—past, distant, obstructed, and so forth. And there is no contact with non-existent things such as the past, since contact requires two bases, and in the absence of a base it cannot occur. Thus the required contact with the object is absent. In the absence of the assisting factor, how could the senses be capable of directly perceiving past objects and the like? And the principle holds: whatever cooperating condition is required for producing a given effect—in its absence, [the cause] does not produce that effect; just as a seed, which requires earth and water as cooperating conditions for producing a sprout, does not produce a sprout in the absence of earth and the like. External senses generate cognition when assisted by contact with the object; therefore, they too do not generate cognition regarding past or future objects, and so the perception produced by them does not transcend the aforementioned restriction of objects. Nor is it produced by the internal organ, since the internal organ is autonomous only with respect to internal objects such as pleasure; if the mind's unrestricted capacity for external objects were accepted, then what would be the use of the eyes and other senses? And then no one would be blind or deaf. And here the principle applies: The mind, which is a matter of dispute, does not operate in the domain of external perception independently of external senses, because in that domain it functions as dependent on them. Whatever functions as dependent on something in a given domain does not operate in that domain independently of it, just as the eye, which functions as dependent on light, does not [function] in its own domain in complete darkness. And it is not possible that senses enhanced through accomplished herbs, the power of austerity, or the glory of <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) ever abandon their established object-restrictions, because such enhancements only result in the manifestation of their inherent capacities, and those capacities are specifically delimited. Indeed, even an ear refined by hundreds of well-applied medicines is not capable of discerning the distinctions of form and taste. And the principle holds: the enhancement of external and internal sensory acuity that is the subject of dispute does not transgress its boundaries, because it is a degree of sensory enhancement, just like the observed degrees of such enhancement. Thus sensory cognition does not make past objects and the like its content.

body.text: bhāvanāprakarṣaparyantajanmanastu satyapi viśadanirbhāsatve prācyānu bhavagocarādanadhikamadhikaṃ vādhyavasyataḥ smṛtivibhramastrotasoranya tarāvartaparivartinaḥ kutaḥ prāmāṇyakūlapratilambhaḥ ? kutastarāṃ ca pratyakṣatayottambhanam ? / pratyakṣasya vā sataḥ kathamiva viditaviṣayaniyamavyatikramaḥ ? atikrāmato vā kutaḥ pratkṣatvamiti na viśvānubhavaiśvaryaśālini pratyakṣaṃ pramāṇam /
body.translated_text: But as for cognition born at the culmination of meditative cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), even though it has vivid manifestation, it ascertains no more than—or at most the same as—what was previously experienced. Whence the attainment of the shore of valid knowledge for the streams of memory and error that revolve in one another's whirlpools? And how much more so the claim to being upheld as perception? Or if it is genuinely perception, how could there be a transgression of its established object-restriction? And if it does transgress, whence its status as perception? Therefore, perception is not a means of valid knowledge regarding one who possesses the sovereignty of universal experience.

children.translated_text: (Thus the rejection of perception as a means of knowledge regarding God.)

body.text: nāpi pramāṇāntaram / tatsvalvanumānamāgamo vā ? anumānamapi viśeṣatodṛṣṭaṃ sāmānyatodṛṣṭaṃ vā ? tatra sakalapadavīdavīyasi bhagavati na tāvatsvalakṣaṇasākṣātkārapūrvakāvinābhāvāvadhāraṇādhīnodayatvādidamanumānamudatumalam / na hyanavagatacarahutabhujastadavinābhāvitayā dhūmamanusandhātumīśate / naca sarvārthanirmāṇasākṣātkārapaṭīyasi liṅgaṃ sāmānyatodṛṣṭamapi kiñcana labhyate/
body.translated_text: Nor [can <s>Īśvara</s> be established by] another <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition). Would that be inference (<s>anumāna</s>) specifically, or scripture (<s>āgama</s>)? And would that inference be <s>viśeṣataḥ dṛṣṭa</s> (based on a particular observed concomitance) or <s>sāmānyataḥ dṛṣṭa</s> (based on a generally observed concomitance)? In the case of the Blessed Lord, who transcends all realms of [ordinary] cognition — first, this inference [of the viśeṣataḥ dṛṣṭa type] is incapable of arising, because its arising depends on the ascertainment of invariable concomitance preceded by the direct perception of the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular). For one who has not apprehended the fire that leaves traces cannot connect smoke with that [fire] as its invariable concomitant. Nor can any mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of the <s>sāmānyataḥ dṛṣṭa</s> type be found for the one most adept at the direct perception of the creation of all things.

children.translated_text: (Thus, the introduction of the impossibility of the validity of inference regarding <s>Īśvara</s>.)

body.translated_text: He himself elucidates the meaning of the verse beginning with 'when it is established' by [the words] 'regarding all objects' and so forth.

body.text: avagamayatā - gṛhṇatā / avagamayanta iti pūrvamudritapāṭho 'śuddhaḥ / deśaviprakarṣo dūradeśasthatvam / kālaviprakarṣo 'tītatvamanāgatatvaṃ ca / svabhāvaviprakarṣo 'yogyatvamatīndriyatvarūpam / yogyānāmapi kuḍyādivyavahitānāṃ cakṣurādināgrahaṇaṃ dṛṣṭam / sarvārtheṣvevambhūtā api padārthāḥ praviṣṭā iti bhāvaḥ / evakāro 'pyarthe / gocarayitavyāni - viṣayīkaraṇīyāni / 'napuṃsakamanapuṃsakene'ti klībaikaśeṣanirdeśo 'yam / ' na ce ' ti / vidyamānetyanena kālaviprakṛṣṭasya vyavacchedaḥ / indriyasannikarṣayogyetyanena vyavahitasya deśaviprakṛṣṭasya ca / katipayetyanenātīndriyasya / katipayaviṣayaniyatavṛtteḥ - niruktavidhakakatipayapadārthamātragrahaṇānuguṇavyāpāravataḥ / niravadhirmahimā apakarṣāsamānādhikaraṇotkarṣaḥ / sa ca jñānasya sarvārthagocaratvarūpaḥ / tat - laukikapratyakṣam / iha - sarvadarśitvādiviśiṣṭa īśvare / sādhanaṃ - pramāṇam / śiṣṭaṃ spaṣṭam /
body.translated_text: 'Apprehending' means 'grasping.' The previously printed reading 'avagamayanta' is incorrect. 'Remoteness of place' means being situated in a distant place. 'Remoteness of time' means being past or future. 'Remoteness of nature' means unsuitability, having the form of being beyond the senses. Even among suitable [objects], it is observed that the eye and other [senses] do not grasp those concealed by walls and the like. The point is that such objects are included among all objects. The particle 'eva' has an emphatic sense. 'To be brought within range' means 'to be made objects of.' This is a <s>ekaśeṣa</s> (singular remainder) statement in the neuter gender according to the rule 'a neuter with a non-neuter.' 'Na ca' ('and not'): by 'existing,' the exclusion of what is remote in time [is indicated]. By 'fit for sensory contact,' [the exclusion of] what is obstructed and remote in place. By 'a few,' [the exclusion of] what is beyond the senses. 'Of limited operation confined to a few objects' means: having an activity suited to the grasping of only a few specific objects as described. 'Unlimited greatness' means: excellence that has no co-location with inferiority. And that [excellence] takes the form of cognition having all objects as its range. 'That' refers to ordinary perception. 'Here' refers to <s>Īśvara</s> qualified by omniscience and so forth. 'Means of establishment' means <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge). The rest is clear.

children.text: yogipratyakṣasyāpīśvarāsādhakatvaṃ sādhayati 'pratyakṣatva' iti / pratyakṣatvavyāpakatvādvartamānārthagrāhakatvasya yogijñānamapi pratyakṣaṃ cedvartamānaikagrāhi
children.translated_text: He establishes that even <s>yogipratyakṣa</s> (yogic perception) is incapable of establishing <s>Īśvara</s>, [beginning with] 'being perception' and so forth. Since being a grasper of present objects alone pervades being perception, yogic cognition too, if it is perception, would grasp only present [objects],

body.text: bhavediti na tasya sarvārthagrāhakatvam / atītādilaviṣayatve vā na tatpratyakṣaṃ bhavet / kintu pratibhādijñānavadupanītabhānaviśeṣarūpameva saṃśayādisahamiti na pramāṇatāmanubhavitumalamīśvara ityarthaḥ//3//
body.translated_text: and thus it would not have the capacity to grasp all objects. Or, if it does have past and future objects in its scope, then it would not be perception, but rather — like <s>pratibhā</s> (intuition) and similar cognitions — it would merely be a special appearance of presented [content], accompanied by doubt and the like, and thus incapable of attaining the status of a <s>pramāṇa</s> regarding <s>Īśvara</s>. This is the meaning. // 3 //
Objection: The world, which is the object of dispute, is dependent on a single conscious being,
because it is begun by something non-conscious — like one's own body, which is free from disease. // 4 //
Moreover, the skill in directly perceiving the creation of all things
should be inferred of that creator, from the mere fact that the world is an effect (<s>kārya</s>). // 5 //

children.text: sarvaṃ hi kāryamupādānopakaraṇasampradānaprayojanasaṃvedicetanaracitamavagataṃ ghaṭamaṇikakagṛhādi / kāryaṃ ca vimatipadamavanigirimahārṇavādīti tadapi
children.translated_text: For every effect is understood to be fashioned by a conscious being who knows the material cause (<s>upādāna</s>), the instruments (<s>upakaraṇa</s>), the recipient (<s>sampradāna</s>), and the purpose (<s>prayojana</s>) — such as pots, jeweled palaces, houses, and the like. And the earth, mountains, great oceans, and so forth, which are the objects of doubt, being effects,

children.text: tathāvidhabuddhimaddhetukamadhyavasīyate / na ca kāryatvamasiddhamiti vācyam , avayavasanniveśādibhirhetubhistatsiddheḥ / iha cāntyāvayavibhyaḥ prabhṛti ādvyaṇukakamakhilamavayavikramanihīyamānanānāvayavavyatiṣaṅgaviśeṣajanitamavagatam ityantata upādānaṃ caturvidhāḥ paramāṇavaḥ prapañcasya / teṣāmādiparispandaśca tadamuguṇādṛṣṭaviśiṣṭatattatkṣetrajñasaṃyogāsamavāyikāraṇakaka iti upakaraṇamapi samastabhetrajñavartīni dharmādharmalakṣaṇānyadṛṣṭāni / prayojanaṃ punastadabhinirvartitavicitrārthakriyākāraścetanopakāraprakārabhedo 'payantaḥ / tadupabhujasta eva kṣetrajñāḥ samprdānam / na cāmī svasamavāyināvapi dharmādharmāvalamavalokayitumiti tadatirekī nikhilabhuvananirmāṇa nipuṇo 'dhikaraṇasiddhāntasamadhigataniratiśayasahajasakalaviṣayasaṃvideśvaryaśakyatyatiśayaḥ puruṣadhaureyakaḥ kimiti na sāmānyatodṛṣṭaliṅgādanumīyate ?
children.translated_text: are also to be inferred as having a cause endowed with such intelligence. Nor should it be said that the effect-nature [of the world] is unestablished, since that [effect-nature] is established by reasons such as the arrangement of parts and the like. Moreover, here, starting from the final composite entities down to the dyads (<s>dvyaṇuka</s>), everything composite is understood to be produced from the specific conjunction of diminishing varieties of constituent parts — and thus, ultimately, the material cause of the manifest world is the four types of atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>). And their initial motion [is caused by] the conjunction of each respective <s>kṣetrajña</s> (individual self), qualified by the <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit/demerit) appropriate to that [motion], serving as the non-inherent cause (<s>asamavāyikāraṇa</s>). And the instruments too are the <s>adṛṣṭas</s> (unseen forces), characterized as <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, residing in all the <s>kṣetrajñas</s>. The purpose, moreover, is the variety of modes of benefit to conscious beings, taking the form of the diverse purposeful activities produced by that [creation]. Those very <s>kṣetrajñas</s> who experience [the fruits] are the recipients. And since these [individual selves] are unable to perceive even their own inherent <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, [there must exist] one who transcends them — a supreme person (<s>puruṣadhaureyaka</s>), skilled in the construction of the entire universe, whose unsurpassable lordship consists in innate, unlimited, all-encompassing consciousness established by the principle of the substrate — why should he not be inferred from the <s>sāmānyataḥ dṛṣṭa</s> (generally observed) mark?

children.text: (itīśvare sāmānyatodṛṣṭānumānasya pramāṇatāpratipādanam) tadidamaviditānumānavṛttasya svamatiracitataralatarkollasitamiti parihasanti mīmāsaṃkāḥ / tathāhi - kimidamekacetanādhīnatvaṃ nāmābhipretaṃ tanubhūvanādeḥ ? tadāyattatvamiti cet ;
children.translated_text: (Thus, the demonstration of the validity of <s>sāmānyataḥ dṛṣṭa</s> inference regarding <s>Īśvara</s>.) 'This is merely the flickering of unsteady reasoning invented by one who does not know the procedure of inference' — thus the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> mock [the argument]. For thus [they ask]: What is this 'dependence on a single conscious being' that is intended regarding the body, the universe, and so forth? If [you mean] its being under the control of that [being] —

children.text: ślokārthameva prapañcayati 'ta' dityādinā / 'samadhigate'tyādi bahuvrīhivṛttam / yaiḥ svayogyārthasannikarṣarūpasahakārikāraṇamadhigatam , evaṃbhūtāni cakṣurādīni
children.translated_text: He elaborates the meaning of the verse itself beginning with 'that' and so forth. 'Samadhigata' and so forth is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> (possessive) compound. By which [sense faculties], the co-operative cause in the form of contact with their proper objects has been ascertained — such sense faculties as the eye and so forth

children.text: svaviṣayapratyakṣajñānajanakānīti loke prasiddhamityarthaḥ / 'ata' iti / yator'thasannikarṣasya sahakāritvaṃ prasiddhamanvayavyatirekābhyām , ata ityarthaḥ / 'rasanādibhi'riti / 'nayanādibhi'riti pāṭhaḥ syādvā / ajātātivṛttau - āgāmyatītau / indriyeṇātītānāgatayoragrahaṇe prayojakaṃ sannikarṣābhāvamupapādayati 'na ce' ti / rajatādibhiriti mudritapāṭhastu na susaṅgataḥ / tasya - sannikarṣasya saṃyogalakṣaṇasya, dvyāśrayatvāt - ubhayasamavāyikatvāt , āśrayābhāve - anyatarāśrayavirahe, tadasambhavāt - sannikarṣotpattyayogāt / 'ataḥ' iti sahakāritvādityarthaḥ / indriyeṇātītādigrahaṇāsambhavamupapādayati sahakārīti / kāraṇābhāvātkāryābhāva iti bhāvaḥ / amumarthaṃ prayogārūḍhaṃ prapañcayati bhavati ceti / yadityādyudāharaṇavākyam / yatsahakāri yasya tadyatsahakārīti bahuvrīhivṛttam / yādṛksahakāriviśiṣṭamityarthaḥ / evamagre 'pi bodhyam / jananam - janakam / arthasannikarṣe tyādyupanayaḥ / tānyapīti nigamanam / indriyāṇi nātītādigrāhīṇi, tadasannikṛṣṭatvāditi pratijñāhetū cānusandheyau / evaṃ yogipratyakṣasyabahirindriyajatve na sarvārthagocaratvamityuktam / ataśceśvare tasya sādhanatvāyogaḥ phalitaḥ /
children.translated_text: are well-known in the world as producing perceptual knowledge of their respective objects. This is the meaning. 'Ataḥ' ('therefore'): the meaning is 'since the co-operative role of contact with the object is well-known through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>), therefore.' 'Rasanādibhiḥ' ('by the tongue and so forth'): or the reading may be 'nayanādibhiḥ' ('by the eye and so forth'). 'Ajātātivṛttau' [means] 'future and past.' He provides the reason for the non-apprehension of past and future by the senses — namely, the absence of contact — beginning with 'na ca.' The printed reading 'rajatādibhiḥ' is not well-fitted. 'Tasya' refers to the contact (<s>sannikarṣa</s>) characterized as conjunction. 'Dvyāśrayatvāt' means 'because it depends on both substrates.' 'Āśrayābhāve' means 'in the absence of one of the two substrates.' 'Tadasambhavāt' means 'because the arising of that contact is impossible.' 'Ataḥ' means 'because of its co-operative role.' He establishes the impossibility of the senses grasping past objects and so forth, [beginning with] 'sahakārī.' The purport is: from the absence of the cause, the absence of the effect. He elaborates this point in the form of a formal proof, [beginning with] 'bhavati ca.' The sentence beginning with 'yat' and so forth is the example. 'Yatsahakāri yasya' is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound meaning 'that which has such-and-such a co-operative [cause].' The meaning is: 'qualified by a co-operative cause of such-and-such a kind.' This should be understood similarly further on. 'Jananam' means 'that which produces.' 'Arthasannikarṣe' and so forth is the application (<s>upanaya</s>). 'Tāny api' and so forth is the conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>). The thesis and reason should be connected thus: 'The senses do not grasp past objects and so forth, because they are not in contact with them.' Thus it has been stated that yogic perception, being of the nature of external sense-cognition, does not have all objects as its scope. And therefore its unsuitability as a means of establishing <s>Īśvara</s> follows.

children.text: atha tasya manomātrajanyatve 'pi na tatpramāṇatvaṃ sarvārthadyagrāhakatvādevetyāha ' nāpyāntare' ti / ' āntaragocara' iti / karmadhārayo 'yam / abāhyaviṣaye sukhādāveva manaso bahirindrayamadvāhīkṛtya pratyakṣajanakatvādityarthaḥ / manasaḥ sākṣādeva bāhyārthagrāhakatve doṣamāha ' niraṅkuśe' ti / niraṅkuśatvamatra bahirindriyanirapekṣatvam / evaṃ manasi hetumupapādya sādhyaṃ prayogamukhataḥ sādhayati ' bhavatī ' ti / prayoga iti śeṣaḥ / na pravartatena grahaṇānuguṇapravṛttimat / tattantravṛttitvāt - bāhyārtheṣu bahirindriyasahakāradvārakagrahaṇavyāpṛtimattvāt / tantraṃ - prayojakaṃ, sahakāri vā / tattantraṃ yasyāḥ, evambhūtā vṛttiryasya tattattantravṛtti, tasya bhāvastattvaṃ tasmāditi ca
children.translated_text: Now, even if [yogic perception] is produced by the mind alone, it is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> because it grasps all objects — this he states beginning with 'nāpy āntare.' 'Āntaragocara' is a <s>karmadhāraya</s> (appositional) compound. The meaning is: regarding internal objects such as pleasure and the like alone, the mind, without employing external sense faculties, produces perceptual knowledge. He states the fault if the mind directly grasps external objects, beginning with 'niraṅkuśe.' 'Unrestrained' here means 'independent of external senses.' Having thus provided the reason regarding the mind, he establishes the thesis through the form of a proof, beginning with 'bhavati.' [The word] 'prayoga' ('formal proof') is to be supplied. 'Does not operate' means: it does not have activity suited to grasping. 'Because its operation belongs to that system' means: because it has the function of grasping external objects through the medium of co-operative external senses. 'Tantra' means 'that which impels,' or 'co-operative [cause].' That whose activity is of such a systemic nature — that is 'tattantravṛtti,' and from its state, 'tattvam,' 'tasmāt' —

body.text: vyutpattiḥ / udāharaṇaṃ ' yadyatre ' ti / yadyatra kārye yatsahakārisamavadhānādhīnajananavyāpāravat tattadasamavadhāne na tatkāryajanakatāvat , yathā'lokasahakārikaṃ jakṣurnālokābhāve svārthaghaṭādicākṣuṣajanakamityarthaḥ / śaṅkate ' na ce ' ti / ājanmasiddherapi prāktanatapaḥ phalatvātpṛthaganuktiratra / siddhauṣadhādisādhyaścendriyāṇāṃ pāṭavātiśayaḥ sūkṣmaviprakṛṣṭādigrahaṇasāmarthyalakṣaṇaḥ /
body.translated_text: this is the derivation. The example is 'yady atra.' [Meaning:] If, in a given effect, [a faculty] has the operation of producing [cognition] dependent on the presence of a given co-operative [cause], then in the absence of that [co-operative cause] it does not have the capacity to produce that effect-cognition — just as the eye, which has light as its co-operative cause, does not produce visual cognition of its proper objects such as pots in the absence of light. This is the meaning. He raises an objection beginning with 'na ca.' The extraordinary acuity of the senses — characterized by the capacity to grasp subtle, remote, and other [objects] — being achievable through perfected herbs and the like, is also not mentioned separately here because it is a result of austerities in previous lives, even though it is established from birth.

children.text:
samadhigataviṣayaniyamam - autsargikaṃ vartamānayogyasannikṛṣṭārthamātragrāhakatvarūpaniyamam / apajahati - parityajanti / pariharati ' sāṃsiddhike ' ti / karmapratibaddhasaṅkucitapravṛttisvābhāvikakaraṇaśaktivikāsakatvameva siddhauṣa dhādīnām , natvapūrvaśaktyādhāyakatvamityarthaḥ / nanvastvevam / tāvatā yogicakṣurādinā sarvārthāgrahaṇasya kimāyātam ? atrāha ' śakteśce ' ti / cakṣuṣo hi svābhāvikaṃ sāmarthyaṃ rūparūpyādigrahaṇa eva, na tu yogādināpi rasādigrahaṇe sāmarthyaṃ tasya saṃbhavatītyarthaḥ / tathāca pāṭavātiśayāddhavīyo 'pi sūkṣmatamaṃ rūpaṃ gṛhṇātu nāma yogicakṣuḥ / naitāvatātītādeḥ rasādervā tadgrāhakaṃ bhavediti bhāvaḥ / atra ca nyāyamāha ' bhavatī' ti / anullaṅghitasīmā - anatikrāntasvamaryādaḥ / maryādā ca cakṣuṣo rūpādiṣu caturṣu rūpasyaiva grāhakatvamiti / evaṃ rasanādāvapi anusandheyam / ' dṛśyamāne ' ti / ayogināmapi cākṣuṣatejomāndyaprakarṣābhyāṃ rūpādigrahaṇatāratamyaṃ hi dṛṣṭam / evameva yogicakṣustejaḥprakarṣo 'pi tato 'pyadhikagocaro 'natikrāntamaryāda eva sidhyedityāśayaḥ / evamaindriyikatve yogijñānasya sarvārthādyagrāhakatvamupapādyānaindriyikatve 'pi tasya yathātvamata eveśvare pramāṇatvāsaṃbhavaṃ copapādayati ' bhāvane ' ti / bhāvanāprakarṣaprayante janma yasyeti bahuvrīhiḥ / viśadanirbhāsatve - viśadaprakāśakatve - laukikaviṣayatānirūpakatve / prācyānubhavagocarāt - pūrvānubhavaviṣayāt / adhyavasyataḥ - prakāśayataḥ / pūrvānubhūtādanadhikaviṣayatve smṛtitvam / adhikaviṣayatve tu bhramatvam , kāminībhāvayituḥ kāminaḥ purovartitvenāsatyāḥ kāminyāḥ pratimānasyevetyarthaḥ / samuditāśayastvayam - anubhūtasya paunaḥpunyena smṛtyabhyāsena saṃskārapracayaḥ saṃpadyate / tatparyante smṛtyabhyāse sati jāyamānā smṛtirevapratyakṣavadviśadaviṣayāvabhāsā bhavatīti pratyakṣasamānākāraṃ smaraṇameva cedyogipratyakṣaṃ vivakṣitam , tarhi tasya pūrvānubhūtārthamātragocaratvānneśvaragocaratvam / sarvārthagrahaṇādisamarthasyeśvarasya pramāṇābhāvena prāgananubhūtatvāt / smṛtitve ca yathārthānubhavatvalakṣaṇamajñātārthajñāpakatvalakṣaṇaṃ vā prāmāṇyaṃ tannārhatyeva / ata eva pramāṇaviśeṣapratyakṣarūpatvaṃ tasya na tarāṃ
ghaṭata iti / ' pratyakṣatve ' iti
children.translated_text: Regarding 'the established restriction of objects' — it abandons the default restriction, which is the nature of grasping only presently capable and proximately connected objects. 'It sets aside' — they relinquish. He addresses this with '<s>sāṃsiddhike</s>' (regarding the innate). The meaning is: the function of <s>siddha</s>-herbs and the like is merely to unfold the natural capacity of the sense-organs whose activity is contracted and bound by <s>karma</s>, not to bestow a previously non-existent power. Let it be so, one might say; but how does it follow that the yogic eye and so forth cannot grasp all objects? To this he responds with '<s>śakteśca</s>' (and of the power). For the natural capacity of the eye is only for grasping color and colored things, and even through <s>yoga</s> and the like, the capacity to grasp taste and so forth is not possible for it — this is the meaning. And thus, through excellence of acuity, let the yogic eye grasp even the most subtle form; but merely by that much it would not become a grasper of past things or of taste and the like — this is the purport. And here he states the principle with '<s>bhavatī</s>' (it becomes). 'Without transgressing the boundary' — not overstepping its own limit. And the limit of the eye among the four [sense-objects] beginning with form is that it grasps only form. The same should be understood regarding the tongue and other sense-organs as well. Regarding '<s>dṛśyamāne</s>' (in what is seen): even for non-yogins, a gradation in the grasping of form and the like is observed due to degrees of weakness and strength of visual luminosity. Just so, even the excellence of luminosity of the yogic eye, though its range exceeds that [of ordinary vision], would be established as not transgressing its boundary — this is the intent. Having thus demonstrated, when yogic cognition is sensory (<s>aindriyika</s>), that it cannot grasp all objects and so forth, he also establishes that even when it is non-sensory, for the very same reason it cannot serve as a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) regarding <s>Īśvara</s>, with '<s>bhāvane</s>' (in meditation). '<s>Bhāvanāprakarṣaparyante janma</s>' is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound meaning 'that whose origin lies at the culmination of intense meditation.' Regarding 'clear manifestation' — regarding the capacity for vivid illumination — regarding the determination of mundane object-hood. 'From the domain of prior experience' — from the object of previous experience. 'Determining' — illuminating. When the object does not exceed what was previously experienced, it is memory (<s>smṛti</s>). When the object exceeds [prior experience], it is error (<s>bhrama</s>), like the mental image of an unreal beloved appearing before one who meditates on a woman — this is the meaning. The assembled purport is this: through repeated recollection-practice of what was experienced, an accumulation of impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) is produced. At the culmination of that recollection-practice, the memory that arises, appearing with vivid object-manifestation like direct perception — if what is intended by 'yogic perception' (<s>yogipratyakṣa</s>) is merely such remembrance resembling direct perception in form, then because it has as its domain only previously experienced objects, it cannot have <s>Īśvara</s> as its object. For <s>Īśvara</s>, who is capable of grasping all objects and so forth, has not been previously experienced due to the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s> [for Him]. And if it is memory, the validity characterized as veridical experience, or characterized as making known what was not previously known, simply does not belong to it. For this very reason, its being of the nature of perception, a particular type of <s>pramāṇa</s>, is all the more untenable. With '<s>pratyakṣatve</s>' (regarding its being perception) —

body.text: ślokārthopasaṃhāraḥ ' pratyakṣasya ve ' ti / viditatvaṃ - prasiddhatvam / ' na viśve ' ti / sarvasākṣātkartari sarvakartari sarvaniyantari ceśvare 'smadādīnāṃ yogināṃ vendriyarūpaṃ pratyakṣaṃ na pramāṇaṃ - na pramitijanakamityarthaḥ / nanu kevalasya bahirasvātantrye 'pi yogajaprakṛṣṭādṛṣṭasahakṛtasya tasya bāhyeṣvatīndriyeṣu traikālikeṣu cārtheṣu pravṛttiḥ saṃbhavennāma / tat prakṛṣṭādṛṣṭasahakṛtamanojanyameva pratyakṣaṃ yogināṃ syādīśvare pramāṇam / pratyakṣasya vartamānamātragrāhitvamiti vyavasthā cāyogipratyakṣaikagocareti cet ; atra brūmaḥ - prakṛṣṭādṛṣṭaviśeṣasahakārādapi prāmāṇikasarvārthagrahaṇameva bhavennāma/ sarveśvare caikasmin na pramāṇaṃ kiñcit / ato na tatsiddhiryogajapratyakṣeṇāpīti hārdamākṣeptuḥ / etena paramātmadhyānajanitameva paramātmaviṣayamānasapratyatraṃ pramāṇaṃ tasminnityapi nirastam / paramātmano dhyānaṃ hi tajjñānamantarā na saṃbhavati / taccāntato gatvā śāstrajanitameveti vaktavyam / śāstrasya ca kāryaparasya na tatra tātparyam / śrutipauruṣeyatvanaye punaranyonyasaṃśrayaḥ spaṣṭa eva īśvarasiddhau taduktatvācchāstraprāmāṇyasiddhiḥ, tatsiddhau ceśvarasiddhiriti / anumānaṃ ca na pramāṇaṃ tatretyanantarameva vakṣyate / tathā ceśvarapramiterevābhāvāttanmūlataddhyānādyasiddhireveti / evaṃ laukikayaugikabhedena dvividhasya pratyakṣasyeśvare na pramāṇatvamityuktam /
body.translated_text: The summary of the verse's meaning is given with '<s>pratyakṣasya va</s>' (or of perception). '<s>Viditatvam</s>' — well-known-ness. With '<s>na viśve</s>' (not in the universal): regarding <s>Īśvara</s>, who is the direct witness of all, the agent of all, and the controller of all — for us and for <s>yogins</s> alike, perception of the sensory kind is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>, that is, it does not generate valid cognition — this is the meaning. But, one might object, even if the [sense-organ] alone lacks independence regarding external objects, that [sense-organ] assisted by potent unseen merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) born of <s>yoga</s> could indeed function with respect to external, supersensory, and objects across all three times. In that case, perception born from <s>manas</s> (mind) assisted by potent <s>adṛṣṭa</s> would be the <s>yogins</s>' perception serving as <s>pramāṇa</s> regarding <s>Īśvara</s>. And the principle that perception grasps only present objects applies only to non-yogic perception — if so, to this we say: even through the assistance of a particular potent <s>adṛṣṭa</s>, let there indeed be authoritative grasping of all objects; still, regarding the one <s>Īśvara</s> who encompasses all, no <s>pramāṇa</s> [is possible]. Therefore, His establishment is not possible even through yogic perception — this is the essential objection. By this, the claim that mental perception (<s>mānasa-pratyakṣa</s>) regarding the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self), generated by meditation on the <s>Paramātman</s>, is a <s>pramāṇa</s> for Him — this too is refuted. For meditation on the <s>Paramātman</s> is not possible without prior knowledge of Him. And that [knowledge] must ultimately be said to originate from scripture (<s>śāstra</s>). And scripture, whose purport concerns effects (<s>kārya</s>), does not have its primary intent there [i.e., in establishing <s>Īśvara</s>]. Moreover, on the view that <s>Śruti</s> (Vedic scripture) is of human authorship (<s>pauruṣeya</s>), there is clearly mutual dependence (<s>anyonyāśraya</s>): the establishment of <s>Īśvara</s> depends on scripture's authority since it is stated therein, and the establishment of scripture's authority depends on <s>Īśvara</s>'s establishment. And that inference too is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> there — this will be stated immediately after. And thus, since there is simply no valid cognition of <s>Īśvara</s> [through these means], the meditation on Him and the like that depend on it are themselves unestablished. Thus it has been stated that perception of both kinds — ordinary (<s>laukika</s>) and yogic (<s>yaugika</s>) — is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> regarding <s>Īśvara</s>.

body.text: kimasya tasminnāyattaṃ kiṃ nu janmāthavā sthitiḥ /
body.translated_text: What depends upon Him in this [world] — is it birth, or is it continued existence?
Or is it the activity of the first two? The example is devoid of what is to be proved. // 6 //

body.text: na khalu śarīramekacetanādhīnotpattisthiti / ye hi yaddehādhīnasukhaduḥkhopabhogabhāginaḥ, bhavati hi taducitādṛṣṭaśālināṃ sarveṣāmeva teṣāṃ taddehina iva tadutpattisthitinimittatvam / api ca śarīrāvayavinaḥ svāvayavasamavāyalakṣaṇā sthitiravayavavyatiṣaṅgaviśeṣādṛte na cetayitāraṃ paramapekṣate / yā punastadapekṣiṇī prāṇanalakṣaṇā sthitiḥ, na sā pakṣīkṛte kṣityādau sambhavatīti sthitimapi naikarūpāṃ pakṣasapakṣānuyāyinīmudīkṣāmahe /
body.translated_text: Indeed, the body's origination and continued existence do not depend on a single conscious being. For those who partake in the experience of pleasure and pain dependent on a particular body — all of them who possess the appropriate unseen merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) have the status of being causes of that body's origination and continued existence, just like the embodied soul [of that body]. Moreover, the continued existence of the composite body, characterized by the inherence of its own parts, does not require an intelligent agent apart from the specific conjunction of its parts. And that continued existence characterized by vital breathing (<s>prāṇana</s>), which does require [an intelligent agent], is not possible in the case under consideration, namely earth and the like — thus we do not find a single uniform type of continued existence that applies consistently to both the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣa</s>) and the corroborating instance (<s>sapakṣa</s>).

body.text: ekacetanādhīnapravṛttitve tu prabalabahujanasarabhasaprayatnapracālyairupalataru rathādibhirvyabhicāraḥ / ārabdhatvādeva caitatsādhyasiddhāvadhikamidamupādāna viśeṣavacanam/
body.translated_text: And regarding the dependence of activity on a single conscious being, there is deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) in the case of stones, trees, chariots, and the like, which are set in motion by the vigorous effort of many powerful persons. And since this [world] has already been established [as an effect], this specification of a particular material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) is excessive for proving what is to be proved.

children.translated_text: 'all'

children.text: ' iti / upādānaṃ-samavāyikāraṇam / upakaraṇaṃ-sahakārarikāraṇam / saṃpradānaṃ-kāryaṃ yadbhogārthaṃ sṛṣṭaṃ, sa upabhoktā / prayojanaṃ-kriyamāṇavastusādhyaṃ phalam / upādānādīnāṃ saṃvedī-sākṣātkartā yaścetanaḥ tena nimittahetunā kriyamāṇaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ ghaṭādikāryamityarthaḥ / maṇiko-mahāghaṭaḥ / etadvākyena kāryatvasya sakartṛkatvavyāpyatvaṃ pratipāditaṃ bhavati / upādānādigocarāparokṣajñāna cikīrṣākṛtimattvaṃ kartṛtvamatra vivakṣitam / upanayanimane '
children.translated_text: — thus. '<s>Upādāna</s>' means the material cause (<s>samavāyi-kāraṇa</s>, inherent cause). '<s>Upakaraṇa</s>' means the auxiliary cause (<s>sahakāri-kāraṇa</s>, cooperative cause). '<s>Saṃpradāna</s>' means the beneficiary — the enjoyer for whose enjoyment the effect is created. '<s>Prayojana</s>' means the fruit (<s>phala</s>) that is to be accomplished by the thing being made. The meaning is: an effect such as a pot is observed to be produced by the efficient cause (<s>nimitta-hetu</s>) — the conscious being who is the direct knower of the material cause and the rest, namely the one who has direct perception of the <s>upādāna</s> and so forth. '<s>Maṇika</s>' means a large pot. By this statement, the pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) of effecthood by the property of having an agent is set forth. The agenthood intended here is: possession of direct knowledge regarding the <s>upādāna</s> and so forth, desire to act (<s>cikīrṣā</s>), and bodily effort (<s>kṛti</s>). In the application and conclusion —
'the effect'

children.text: 'ti / vimatipadaṃ sakartṛkatvākartṛkatvavipratipattiviṣayībhūtam / anena sandigdhasādhyakatvalakṣaṇaṃ pakṣatvamavanyāderupapannamiti sūcitam / svarūpāsiddhimāśaṅkya pariharati '
children.translated_text: — thus. The subject of doubt (<s>vimati-pada</s>) is the locus of conflicting views regarding whether [the world] has an agent or is without an agent. By this it is indicated that the status of being a thesis (<s>pakṣatva</s>) — characterized by having the property-to-be-proved in doubt — is well established in the case of the earth and so forth. Anticipating the objection of the unestablished nature of the subject itself (<s>svarūpāsiddhi</s>), he resolves it with —
'not'

children.text: ' ti / pakṣe mahyādāviti śeṣaḥ / ākṛtimattvādibhiḥ kṣityādeḥ kāryatvasiddhiriti bhāvaḥ / pakṣadharmatābalātkartṛviśeṣasiddhiriti pratipādanārthaṃ kāryasāmānyopādānādi nirdhārayati '
children.translated_text: — thus. The remainder is: 'in the thesis-subject, namely earth and the like.' The purport is that the effecthood of earth and the like is established through [properties such as] having a definite form (<s>ākṛtimatva</s>) and so forth. In order to demonstrate that the specific agent is established by force of the property's presence in the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>), he determines the <s>upādāna</s> and so forth of effects in general, with —
'here'

children.text: ' ti / avayavatvāsamānādhikaraṇāvayavitvāmantyāvayavitvam / antyāvayavita ārabhyādyāvayavidvyaṇukamabhivyāpya sarvamavayavikāryadravyajāta mavayavasaṃyogaviśeṣajanitaṃ prasiddhamityarthaḥ / uttarottarāpekṣayā pūrvapūrvakārye 'vayavālpatvaṃ 'kramanihīyamāne'-tyucyate / avayavasaṃśleṣaviśeṣajanitatvaṃ ca kvacitpratyakṣādanumānāccakvacit siddhamiti bhāvaḥ / antyepādanatvam avayavitvāsamānādhikaraṇāvayavatvam / caturvidhāḥ paramāṇavaḥ pṛthivījalajvalanapavanaparamāṇavaḥ / prapañcasya-kāryadravyaprapañcasya / '
children.translated_text: — thus. The meaning of 'ultimate composite' (<s>antyāvayavitva</s>) is: being a composite that is not co-located with the property of being a part, [i.e., being an ultimate whole]. Starting from the ultimate composite, extending through the first composite [stage], namely the dyad (<s>dvyaṇuka</s>), the entire class of composite-effect substances is well known to be produced by specific conjunctions of parts — this is the meaning. The diminishing number of parts in each successively prior effect is expressed by '<s>kramanihīyamāne</s>' (progressively diminishing). And that [these composites] are produced by specific conjunctions of parts is established in some cases through direct perception and in other cases through inference — this is the purport. The status of being the ultimate material cause is: being a part that is not co-located with composite-hood. The four kinds of <s>paramāṇus</s> (atoms) are: earth-atoms, water-atoms, fire-atoms, and air-atoms. '<s>Prapañca</s>' here means the manifold array of effect-substances. With —
'of those'

children.text: ' miti / paramāṇūnāmādiparispandaḥsargādyakālīnārambhakasaṃyogajanakakriyālakṣaṇaḥ adṛṣṭa vadātmasaṃyogarūpāsamavāyihetuja ityadṛṣṭānāmupakaraṇatvamityarthaḥ / ādyaparispandasyādṛṣṭahetukatvaṃ ca kaṇādamuninā sūtritam '
children.translated_text: — thus. The initial movement (<s>ādyaparispanda</s>) of the atoms — characterized as the action that generates the conjunction which initiates creation at the beginning of a cosmic cycle — is caused by <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit/demerit), being produced by a non-inherent cause (<s>asamavāyi-hetu</s>) in the form of the conjunction of <s>adṛṣṭa</s> with the <s>ātman</s> (self). Thus the <s>adṛṣṭas</s> serve as auxiliary causes (<s>upakaraṇa</s>) — this is the meaning. And that the initial movement is caused by <s>adṛṣṭa</s> has been stated in a <s>sūtra</s> by the sage <s>Kaṇāda</s> —
'The upward flaming of fire, the sideward blowing of wind, and the initial motion of atoms and of <s>manas</s> (mind) are caused by <s>adṛṣṭa</s>'
— thus. With —
'the purpose'

children.text:
'miti / sṛṣṭiprayojanamanavadhirjīvopakāra prakārabhedaḥ sṛjyapadārthanirvāhyanānāvidhārthakriyārūpaḥ nānāvidhabhoganiṣpādana lakṣaṇo 'saṅkhyāta ityarthaḥ/ sampradānaṃ ca sākṣātparamparayā vā kāryapadārthaniṣpāditaṃ
bhogamanubhavanto jīvarāśaya ityāha '
children.translated_text: — thus. The purpose of creation consists in the benefit of <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) in its infinite variety of forms, being of the nature of manifold purposeful activities that sustain the various objects to be created, characterized by the production of manifold enjoyments — [these are] innumerable, is the meaning. And the recipients — the masses of <s>jīvas</s> who experience the enjoyment produced by the effect-objects, directly or indirectly — this is stated [by the verse]:
'those who enjoy that'

children.text: ' iti / evaṃ sarvavidhaparamāṇusarvajīvādṛṣṭasarvajīvopakāraprakārarūpanikhila jagadupādānopakaraṇa- prayojanasākṣātkartṛtvādi jīveṣi na sa bhavatīti kaimutikanyāyena sādhayituṃ svīyādṛṣṭāsākṣātkartṛtvamapi na teṣvityāha '
children.translated_text: — thus. In this way, in order to establish by the argument <s>a fortiori</s> (<s>kaimutika nyāya</s>) that direct agency regarding the material cause of the entire world — in the form of all types of atoms, the <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit) of all <s>jīvas</s>, and the modes of benefiting all <s>jīvas</s>, and the instruments and purposes [of creation] — does not belong to the <s>jīvas</s>, he states that even direct agency over their own <s>adṛṣṭa</s> does not belong to them:
'nor do these'
— thus. [The creator is] distinct from these — different from the <s>jīvas</s>.
'That whose establishment leads to the establishment of another topic — that is the <s>adhikaraṇasiddhānta</s> (principle established incidentally)'

children.text:
'iti nyāyasūtram / yatsiddhimantarā prakṛtor'thoṃ na sidhyati, tathābhūtaḥ prakṛtārthasiddhernāntarīyakatayā sidhyannartho 'dhikaraṇasiddhāntasiddha ityarthaḥ / tathācanikhilārthasākṣātkāritvādyantarā kartṛḥ kṣityādeḥ sakartṛkatvarūpaḥ prakṛtārtho na sidhyatīti viśiṣṭakartṛlābho 'dhikaraṇasiddhāntanayeneti phalitam /
tārkikābhimatamīśvarānumānaprakāramimaṃ nirasyanti mīmāṃsakāḥ '
children.translated_text: — this is the <s>Nyāyasūtra</s>. That without whose establishment the intended matter cannot be established — such a matter, being established as inseparable from the establishment of the intended matter, is called established by the principle of incidental establishment — this is the meaning. And thus, without the establishment of direct perception of all objects and so forth, the intended matter — namely, the fact that earth and the like have a maker — cannot be established. Therefore, the obtaining of a distinguished maker [is established] by the method of incidental establishment — this is the conclusion. The <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> reject this mode of inferring <s>Īśvara</s> (God) accepted by the logicians (<s>Tārkikas</s>):
'This'

children.text: ' mityādinā / dṛṣṭājātīyasyaiva sādhakamanumānaṃ, na tvatīndriyārthasyetyanumānavṛttamajānataḥ svabuddhyatprekṣitāvyavasthitatarkābhāsa mūlamidaṃvilakṣaṇapuruṣasādhanamityarthaḥ / tarkasvabhāvānabhijñasya tārkikatvavyapadeśaḥsuśobhana iti copahāso garbhitaḥ / paroktasya tarkasyābhāsatvamupapādayitumupakramate '
children.translated_text: — with this and what follows. Inference is probative only of things belonging to a class that has been observed, not of supersensible objects — this is a baseless pseudo-reasoning, a groundless arbitrary determination fabricated by one's own intellect, by one who does not know the proper scope of inference; this [argument] for proving a unique being is [merely an appearance] rooted in pseudo-reasoning — this is the meaning. And there is an implicit mockery: how fitting is the designation 'logician' (<s>Tārkika</s>) for one ignorant of the true nature of reasoning! He begins to demonstrate the pseudo-nature of the opponent's reasoning:
'For'
— thus.
'What is this'

children.text: ' iti / tanumuvanādeḥ-piṇḍabrahmāṇḍādeḥ / piṇḍo dehaḥ / tathāca purāṇaratne '
children.translated_text: — thus. Of the body, universe, and so forth — 'body' means the physical form; and thus in the Jewel of <s>Purāṇas</s>:
'The body (<s>piṇḍa</s>) is that which is separate for each person, characterized by head, hands, and so forth'

children.text:
'iti / pakṣasapakṣayoriti vār'thaḥ /
ekacetanāyattatvaṃ jagato vikalpya dūṣayati '
children.translated_text: — thus. The meaning is: of both the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>) and the corroborating instance (<s>sapakṣa</s>). He hypothesizes and refutes the dependence of the world on a single conscious being:
'Is this its'

children.text: ' ti kārikayā / āyattaṃ-kāryatvena saṃbaddham / ekacetanahetukatvaṃ kiṃ bhuvanajanmanaḥ sādhyate, uta bhuvanasthiteḥ, āhosvidbhuvanapravṛtteḥ ? ādyayoḥ kalpayoranvayadṛṣṭānto nīrogadehaḥ sādhyavikala ityarthaḥ / tathāca vyāptyasiddhirvyabhicāraśceti bhāvaḥ // 6 //
children.translated_text: — by this verse. 'Dependent' means connected as an effect. Is the dependence on a single conscious being to be proved of the origin of the world, or of the world's persistence, or of the world's functioning? In the first two alternatives, the corroborating instance — a healthy body — is devoid of the property to be proved, is the meaning. And thus there is non-establishment of pervasion and deviation — this is the purport. // 6 //

body.translated_text: He clarifies the manner in which the specific form of the intended <s>Īśvara</s> is established through this inference, with —
If mere dependence on a conscious being is to be proved, then what is to be proved is already established (<s>siddhasādhyatā</s>);
for, according to us, the object of enjoyment (<s>bhogya</s>) is produced by <s>karmas</s> (actions) for the conscious enjoyers (<s>bhoktṛ</s>). // 7 //

body.text: yuktaṃ caitat-yadubhayavādisiddhānāmeva cetanānāṃ kartṛtvābhyupagamaḥ lāghavāt / na copādānādyanabhijñatayā tatpratikṣepaḥ /
body.translated_text: And this is proper — that agency be accepted only of conscious beings that are already established by both parties, because of the principle of parsimony (<s>lāghava</s>). Nor should this be rejected on the ground of ignorance of the material cause and so forth.

children.translated_text: 'Surely not'

children.text: ' tyādinā / svaśarīrotpattisthityoḥ svasyāpyadṛṣṭadvārā hetutvaṃ vācyam / taccharīrādhīnopabhogopakārabhājāmanyeṣāṃ ca tatrādṛṣṭadvārā hetutvaṃ taddehina ivāstīti ekacetanāyattotpattisthitikatvaṃ dṛṣṭānte nāstītyarthaḥ / dvitīye kalpe sthitiśabdārthavikalpanamukhena dūṣaṇāntaramapyāha '
children.translated_text: — with this and what follows. It should be said that even of one's own body, in its origination and persistence, one's own causality [operates] through the medium of <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit). And others who share in the enjoyment that depends on that body also have causality through the medium of <s>adṛṣṭa</s>, just as the owner of that body does. Therefore, origination and persistence dependent on a single conscious being do not exist in the corroborating instance — this is the meaning. In the second alternative, he states yet another refutation through an analysis of the meaning of the word 'persistence':
'Moreover'

children.text:
' ti/ śarīrāvayavuna iti
karmadhārayavṛttam / ārambhakasaṃyoge 'vayavasamavete dṛḍhe sati svāvayavasamavetatvalakṣaṇāvayavinaḥ sthitiḥ śarīrasya nirābādhā ghaṭāderiva prasidhyatyeveti
naivaṃvidhasthiteścetanāpekṣatā / prāṇavṛttyadhīnāśaithilyāvasthānalakṣaṇā śarīradhṛtiḥ paraṃ jīvanayoniyatnahetukatvādbhavennāma cetanāpekṣā dṛṣṭānte vyāpakatvena sādhanasya gṛhītaivaṃvidhā sthitistu na pakṣe mahyādau / tathāca kāryatvāvacchedena evaṃvidhaikacetanādhīnāsthitikatvasādhaneṃ'śato bādha iti bhāvaḥ / tṛtīye kalpe ekacetanāyattapravṛttikatve 'naikānyamāha '
children.translated_text: — thus. 'Of the body's parts' — this is a <s>karmadhāraya</s> compound. When the originating conjunction of parts — the conjunction inherent in the parts — is firm, the persistence of the whole that has the characteristic of being inherent in its own parts is established without obstruction, just as for a pot and the like. Therefore, persistence of this kind does not require a conscious being. The maintenance of the body — characterized by the loosening or sustaining [of parts] dependent on the vital functions — might indeed require a conscious being, since it is caused by the effort of the living soul. But such persistence in the broader sense, which is grasped as pervading the corroborating instance, does not exist in the thesis — namely, the earth and so forth. And thus, in proving dependence on a single conscious being for this type of persistence delimited by being an effect, there is partial obstruction — this is the purport. In the third alternative — dependence on a single conscious being for functioning — he states the absence of exclusiveness:
'Some'

children.text: ' ti / sarabhasaprayatnaḥ-tīvraprayatnaḥ / bahujanaikasādhyacalanapravṛttimati mahopalādau sādhyaśūnye sattvādanekāntatā hetorityarthaḥ / hetorvyarthaviśeṣaṇatvaṃ cāha '
children.translated_text: — thus. 'With violent effort' means with intense effort. In [objects like] large boulders and the like, whose movement is achievable only by many people, the corroborating instance is devoid of the property to be proved, and therefore the reason is inconclusive due to [the counter-example] being present — this is the meaning. And he states the purposelessness of the qualifier of the reason:
'Merely because it is produced'

children.text:
' ti / janyatvasyaiva hetutve vyabhicārāprasakteracetanopādānanirūpitatvasya tadviśeṣaṇasya vaiyarthyam / tathā ca vyāpyatvāsiddhiḥ / adhikaṃ nāma nigrahasthānaṃ ca prayuñjata iti bhāvaḥ / yadyapi samavetadravyatvarūpe phalite hetau na vaiyarthya prasaktiḥ / athāpi yathāśrutahetvabhiprāyeṇa vyarthaviśeṣaṇatvābidhanam / phalite 'pi hetāvanaikānyaṃ tu durvārameveti dik /
nanvanaikāntyaprasaṅgādekatvaviśeṣaṇaṃ tyajyate / cetanādhīnatvameva tu sādhyata iti cettatrāha '
children.translated_text: — thus. Since 'being produced' alone suffices as the reason, and since deviation does not threaten [with that alone], the qualifier 'being determined as having an unconscious material cause' is purposeless. And thus there is non-establishment of pervasion. Moreover, there is [here] what is called a point of defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>) in the application [of the argument] — this is the purport. Although in the implied reason — having the form 'being an entity inherent in substance' — purposelessness does not threaten, still, the statement of purposeless qualification is [made] in accordance with the intended meaning of the reason as literally stated. And the inconclusiveness even in the implied reason is indeed unavoidable — this is the indication.
'Conscious being'

children.text: ' ti / yadyapyuktahānyādyevaṃ vadataḥ prasajyata eva / athāpi tasyaktidoṣatvattadupekṣyārthadūṣaṇamevātrocyate / '
children.translated_text: — thus. Even though the faults of abandonment and so on apply to one who speaks thus, still, since [the opponent's argument] has this defect, disregarding it, only the refutation of the substance is stated here.
'Indeed'

children.text: ' ti prasiddhau / asmākamapi kāryasāmānyasya jīvādṛṣṭahetukatvena cetanādhīnatvasya sampratipatteḥ cetanādhīnatvamātrasādhane jīvaiḥ sdidhasādhanam / bhavataścārthāntaramiti bhāvaḥ // 7//
children.translated_text: — in the sense of 'it is well-known.' Since we too accept that the generality of effects is dependent on a conscious being, in the sense of being caused by the <s>adṛṣṭa</s> of <s>jīvas</s> — in proving mere dependence on a conscious being, [the conclusion] is already established by the <s>jīvas</s>. And for you [the opponent], it would be a different matter — this is the purport. // 7 //

body.translated_text: He demonstrates the absence of the property to be proved in the corroborating instance:
The material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) is earth and the like; the instrumental cause (<s>sādhana</s>) is sacrifice, gifts, and so forth;

body.text: sākṣātkartuṃ kṣamante yatsarva eva ca cetanāḥ // 8 //
body.translated_text: all conscious beings are capable of directly perceiving that [cause]. // 8 //

body.text: adyavadeva viśvambharādayaḥ karmaprāptāgantukopacayāpacayaikadeśaśālino na yugapadeva niravaśeṣavilayajananabhāgina ityantimaparamāṇusākṣātkāro na kartṛbhāvopayogī /
body.translated_text: Just as at present, the earth-bearers and the like, possessing adventitious accretion and diminution of parts acquired through <s>karma</s>, do not undergo complete dissolution and origination all at once — therefore, the direct perception of the ultimate atoms is not useful for establishing agency.

body.text: nanvadṛṣṭadvārā cenaprayojyatvamātraṃ na sādhyate/ kiṃ tu cetanakartṛkatvam / kartṛtvaṃ ca kṣityādau jīvānāṃ nasaṃbhavatīti cet ; evaṃ sati dvitīyānumāna eva viśrāntiḥ / tatrāpi siddhasādhanamevetyāha'

children.translated_text: 'Proper'

children.text: 'miti / lāghavapakṣapātitvādanumānasya sakartṛkatvānumānasyāpi saṃpratipannajīva mātraviśrāntiriti bhāvaḥ / nanu jīvasya jagatkartṛtvamanupannam / anupapanne cārthe lāghavamakiñcitkaram / tadīśvarasiddhirapratyūheti śaṅkāṃ pratikṣipati '
children.translated_text: — thus. Since inference favors the side of parsimony, even the inference of agency rests with the already-accepted <s>jīvas</s> alone — this is the purport. Objection: the world-creatorship of the <s>jīva</s> is untenable; and where a matter is untenable, parsimony is of no avail; therefore, the establishment of <s>Īśvara</s> (God) is unobstructed — he rejects this doubt:
'Nor regarding the material cause'
— thus. He says that direct perception of the material cause and so forth is indeed possible even for the <s>jīva</s>:
'The material cause'

children.text: 'miti / ayamāśayaḥ-tattadvaidikakarmaṇo 'tiśayitatattatphalasādhanatvamavagatya vedādvaidikānāṃ vacanācca tadanugrahata evānuṣṭhāya tattatkarma yathāvidhi samadhigatasāmarthyaviśeṣā jīvaviśeṣā eva pṛthivyādibhūtacatuṣṭayaṃ bhautikakāryavargopādānabhūtaṃ sahakārivargaṃ ca sākṣātkṛtyopādāya ca jagatsṛjeyuriti na kartrantarakalpanāvakāśa iti / yat yasmāt, kṣamante, atona tatpratikṣepa ityanvayaḥ pūrveṇa // 8 //
children.translated_text: — thus. This is the purport: having understood from the <s>Veda</s> and from the words of Vedic [authorities] that the respective Vedic rituals are the means for attaining their respective exalted results, and having performed those rituals in accordance with that grace, particular <s>jīvas</s> who have attained particular powers through the proper performance of their respective rituals could themselves directly perceive the four elements — earth and the like — which serve as the material cause of the class of material effects, along with the class of auxiliary causes, and having taken them up, they could create the world. Therefore there is no occasion for positing another creator — this is [the argument]. Since (<s>yat</s>) 'they are capable' (<s>kṣamante</s>) of that, therefore there is no rejection of it — this is the syntactic connection with the previous [verse]. // 8 //

body.translated_text: Objection: even if [it is argued that] through the medium of <s>adṛṣṭa</s>, mere [indirect] instrumentality is not what is to be proved, but rather agency by a conscious being — and agency over earth and the like is not possible for <s>jīvas</s>? If so, then there is reliance on the second inference. Even there, [the conclusion] is already established — he says:
That which is the power-nature of <s>karma</s> (action), the basis of [the concept of] <s>apūrva</s> and the like —
let there be no direct perceptibility of that [power]; [but] an entity possessing power is within the range of perception. // 9 //

children.text: na khalu kulālādayaḥ kumbhādikāryamārabhamāṇāstadupādānopakaraṇa- bhūtamṛddaṇḍacakrādikāryotpādanaśaktiṃ sākṣātkṛtya tattadārabhante / yadi paraṃ śaktimaviduṣāmabhilaṣitasādhane tadupādānādivyavahāro 'nupapannaḥ, iha tu-
children.translated_text: Indeed, potters and the like, when producing effects such as pots, do not directly perceive the capacity to produce the effects — namely, [the capacity] of clay, stick, wheel, and the like, which serve as the material cause and instruments — and yet they proceed to produce the respective [effects]. If, however, one objects that the activity of taking up the material cause and so forth is untenable for those who do not know the [inherent] power, then here —

children.text: nanu pralaye pṛthvyāderādyadvyaṇukaṃ vināśājjīvānāṃ ca tadā karaṇakale varavidhuratvena jñānopādānasāmarthyavirahānna teṣāṃ sargādyajagatsṛṣṭikartṛtvaṃ saṃbhavatatyatrāha '
children.translated_text: Objection: at the time of dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>), since the first dyad of earth and the like perishes, and since the <s>jīvas</s> at that time, being bereft of instruments of knowledge due to the absence of a body, lack the capacity for knowledge and [direct] apprehension of the material cause — therefore their creatorship of the world, i.e., creation at the beginning of a new cycle, is not possible. To this he says:
'Just as at present'

children.text:
' diti/ na pṛthivyādīnāṃ sarvāśena pralayotpādau / kintu vartamāna iva kāle bhāgabhedenaiva tau kramaśaḥ / āgantukaikadeśavṛddhihrāsalakṣaṇau / tathāca jīveṣveva keṣāñcitsādhanaviśeṣasamāsāditajñānaśaktyatiśayānāṃ hīnāṃśaprapūraṇātmakaṃ sarjanaṃ pṛthivyādyupādānasākṣātkārāditaḥ saṃbhavedeva viśvāmitrādīnāmivetyarthaḥ / niravaśeṣapralaye na punaḥsargaḥ / sāvaśeṣalaye tu jīvaviśeṣāṇāṃ tattadbhāgabhedakartṛtvaṃ saṃbhaviṣyatīti neśvarakalpanāvasara iti bhāvaḥ/
nanvadṛṣṭamapyasti sahakāri puṇyapāparūpam / tatsākṣātākaramanrā ca na tadanuguṇakāryasarjanaṃ saṃbhavet / tatsākṣātkāro na ca jīvānāṃ ghaṭata ityatrāha '
children.translated_text: [...] Thus, the dissolution and origination of earth and so forth do not occur in their entirety, but rather — just as in the present time — they occur gradually, through divisions of parts alone, characterized by the adventitious increase and decrease of particular portions. Accordingly, among certain individual souls (<s>jīvas</s>) who have acquired extraordinary powers of knowledge through special means, creation in the form of supplementing the diminished portions could indeed be possible from the direct perception of the material causes such as earth and so forth — just like [the creations of] <s>Viśvāmitra</s> and others. This is the meaning. In a complete dissolution, there would be no re-creation. But in a partial dissolution, it would be possible for particular individual souls to be the creators of their respective portions — thus there is no occasion for postulating <s>Īśvara</s>. This is the purport. Objection: But there is also the unseen (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>), in the form of merit and demerit, as a co-operative cause. Without the direct perception of that, creation conforming to it would not be possible. And the direct perception of that is not possible for individual souls — to this he responds:
'Of <s>karma</s>'

children.text:
' iti / anyakartṛkayāgādidharmāṇāṃ cauryādyadharmāṇāṃ ca sākṣātkāre
kṣamā eva sākṣibhūtājīvaviśeṣāḥ / śāsrataśca tattatkarmaṇaḥ phalaviśeṣajanana sāmarthyamadhigatavantaste / tathāca tattadanuguṇaṃ sṛjeyurnāma/ śaktimataḥ sākṣātkāraḥ śakterjñānamātraṃ ca kartṛtvopayogi, natu śakterapi sākṣātkaraṇam / svasya punaḥ / karaṇasāmarthyaṃ cāpekṣitam / tathāca puṇyapāpaśabditakarmaśaktyasākṣātkāre 'pi noparodhaḥ kartabhāvasyeti bhāvaḥ // 9 //
children.translated_text: and so forth. Certain special individual souls who serve as witnesses are indeed capable of directly perceiving the <s>dharma</s> (merit) of sacrifices and the like performed by others, and the <s>adharma</s> (demerit) of theft and the like. And through scripture, they have ascertained the capacity of each respective <s>karma</s> to produce specific results. Accordingly, they could create [the world] in conformity with those [karmic results]. For one who possesses power, direct perception, and the knowledge of that power alone are useful for agency — not the direct perception of the power itself. Moreover, one's own instrumental capacity is also required. Accordingly, even without the direct perception of the power designated by the words 'merit' (<s>puṇya</s>) and 'demerit' (<s>pāpa</s>), there is no obstruction to the state of being a creator. This is the purport. // 9 //

body.translated_text: The diverse powers of <s>karma</s> are understood from scripture (<s>āgama</s>);
therefore, let the individual selves, through [their] <s>karmas</s>, create their own [portions of the world] separately. // 10 //

body.text: api ca tadeva cetanakartṛkaṃ jagati paridṛśyate, yadeva śakyakriyaṃ śakyajñānopādānādi ca / na ca tathā mahīmahīdharamahārṇavādīti kathamiva tattatkāryatvam ? kathantarāṃ ca tadupādānopakaraṇādeḥ sākṣātkāragocaratā ? yādṛśaṃ hi kāryamupādānādyabhijñapūrvakamavagataṃ ghaṭamaṇikādi, tādṛśameva hi tathāvidhabuddhimaddhetukatvānumānāya prabhavati /
body.translated_text: Moreover, only that which has a capacity for [its particular] action and whose material cause and so forth are capable of being known is observed in the world as having a conscious creator. But earth, mountains, great oceans, and the like are not like that — so how can their effect-nature be [established]? And how, furthermore, can the material causes and instruments of those [cosmic entities] fall within the range of direct perception? For only such effects as are understood to be preceded by knowledge of the material cause and so forth — pots, jeweled palaces, and the like — are capable of serving as the basis for inferring a cause endowed with such intelligence.

body.text: api cānīśvareṇa parimitaśaktijñānena vigrahavatānavāptakāmena kṛtamavagataṃ ghaṭādikāryamiti tathāvidhaṃ boddhāramupasthāpayan heturabhimatapuruṣa sārvajñyasarvaiśvaryādiviparyayasādhānādviruddhaḥ syāt / na caivaṃ sati sarvānumānavyavahārocchedaprasaṅga śaṅkitavyaḥ / pramāṇāntaragocare hi liṅgini liṅgabalādāpatato viparītaviśeṣāṃstatpramāṇameva pratiruṇāddhi / iha punaratipatitasakalamānāntarakarmabhāve sarvanirmāṇanipuṇe siṣādhayiṣite yāvanto 'nvayavyatirekāvadhāritāvinābhāvabhājodharmāstānapyaviśeṣeṇopasthāpa yati /
body.translated_text: Moreover, the effect such as a pot that has been understood [to be created] was created by a non-omniscient being with limited power and knowledge, who is embodied and whose desires are unfulfilled. Thus, a reason that presents a knower of such a type — [namely, the reason of] effect-nature — would be contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), since it would establish the opposite of the intended [attributes of] omniscience, supreme lordship, and so forth of the [intended] supreme person. Nor should it be objected that this would lead to the absurd consequence of the destruction of all inferential practice. For when the mark-bearer (<s>liṅgin</s>) is within the range of another <s>pramāṇa</s>, that very <s>pramāṇa</s> blocks the contrary particulars that threaten to arise from the force of the mark (<s>liṅga</s>). But here, when the intended [entity to be proved] — one skilled in the creation of everything — surpasses the scope of all other <s>pramāṇas</s>, whatever properties share the invariable concomitance ascertained through positive and negative concomitance, the [inference] presents all of them without distinction.

children.translated_text: 'na'

children.text: ' ti / tuśabdārthe 'yaṃ prayukto 'yaṃ / yadvā ihetyataḥ pūrvaṃ
children.translated_text: and so forth. The particle 'tu' is used in the sense of [emphasis]. Alternatively, before 'iha,'
'indeed,'
should be construed.
'From scripture (<s>āgama</s>)'

children.text: ' diti/ tena-karmaniṣṭhaśaktīnāṃ śāsrato 'vagamena, karmabhiḥ-nānājīvīyakarmahetutaḥ, karmānuguṇamiti yāvat, ātmānaḥ-śaktimanto jīvāḥ, pṛthak-vibhāgena, tattadekeśabhedeneti yāvat, sarvaṃ jagatkāryadravyajātam, nirmimatām-sṛjantu ityarthaḥ // 10 //
children.translated_text: and so forth. 'Tena' — through the understanding from scripture of the powers residing in <s>karma</s>; 'karmabhiḥ' — on the basis of the <s>karmas</s> belonging to various individual souls, i.e., in conformity with [those] <s>karmas</s>; 'ātmānaḥ' — the individual souls possessing power; 'pṛthak' — separately, i.e., through the division into respective portions; [let them create] the entire collection of world-effect substances; 'nirmimatām' — let them create. This is the meaning. // 10 //

body.translated_text: He demonstrates this very point through an illustration, beginning with
Moreover: the activities of deliberate agents are pervaded by self-interest or compassion.
Since both are absent in <s>Īśvara</s>, the creation of the world is not justified. // 11 //

children.text: avāptakāmatvānna tāvadātmārthe sṛjati ; pralayasamaye pralīnasakalakaraṇakalevarādibhogopakaraṇatayā ca cetanānāṃ duḥkhābhāvāt duḥkhidarśanajanitakṛpāprayuktirapi nāstīti vyāpakabhūtasvārthakāruṇya
children.translated_text: Since his desires are fulfilled (<s>avāptakāma</s>), he does not create for his own sake. And since at the time of dissolution, all instruments of experience such as sense organs, bodies, and the like of conscious beings are dissolved, there is no suffering of conscious beings, and hence there is no compassion motivated by seeing the suffering [of others]. Thus, with the cessation of what pervades [purposeful activity] — namely, self-interest or compassion —

body.translated_text: the pervaded — namely, the activity of a deliberate agent — must also cease.

children.translated_text: 'Moreover'

children.text: ' tyādinā / tatrādau svarūpāsiddhirupādhimukhena vyāpyatvāsiddhiśca kīrtyete / śakyā kriyā-karaṇaṃ yasya tacchakyakrayam / kartṛṃ śakyamiti yāvat / śakyaṃ jñānaṃ yasya tacchakyajñānam, śakyajñānāmupādānādi yasya kāryasya tacchakyajñānopādānādi / evaṃbhūtameva kāryaṃ sakartṛkaṃ bhavitumarhatītyarthaḥ / cetanakartṛkatvarahitaṃ kāryaṃ nāstīti cānusandhem / '
children.translated_text: and so forth. Therein, first, non-establishment of the own-nature (<s>svarūpāsiddhi</s>) and non-establishment of pervasion through a limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>) are declared. 'Śakyā kriyā' — that whose action is possible, i.e., capable of being made; i.e., capable of having a maker. 'Śakyaṃ jñānaṃ' — that whose knowledge is possible, i.e., whose material cause and so forth is of knowable nature. The meaning is: only an effect of such a nature is fit to have a [conscious] maker. And [one should] also connect: there is no effect devoid of a conscious maker.
'Na ca'

children.text: ' ti / tattatkāryatvam-tasya tasya kāryatvaṃ kṣityāderaśakyakriyasyetyarthaḥ / anena svarūpāsiddhirbhāgāsiddhirvāktā / '
children.translated_text: and so forth. 'Tattatkāryatvam' — the effect-nature of this or that, namely, of earth and the like, whose action is not [humanly] possible. This is the meaning. By this, non-establishment of own-nature or non-establishment of a portion [of the thesis] is stated.
'Kathantarām'

children.text: ' miti / upādānopakaraṇaparamāṇvadṛṣṭādeḥsākṣātkartumaśakyatayopādānādisākṣātkāracikīrṣākṛtimatpuruṣapūrvakatvaṃ kathantarāṃ ghaṭate kṣitidvyaṇukāderityarthaḥ / kṣityādeḥ kāryatve cedāgrahaḥ , iṣyatām / sakartṛkatvaṃ tu upapannameveti(?) bhāvaḥ / sopādhikatvamāha '
children.translated_text: and so forth. The meaning is: since the material cause such as atoms and the unseen (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) cannot be directly perceived, how can the being preceded by a person who desires to directly perceive the material cause and so forth be coherent for earth, dyads (<s>dvyaṇuka</s>), and the like? If [one objects:] let the effect-nature of earth and so forth be conceded — [the reply is:] but having a [conscious] maker is indeed established. This is the purport. He states the limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>), beginning with
'Of such a kind'

children.text:
' iti / yādṛśaṃ-kṛtisādhyatvārhaṃ jñeyatvārhepādānādikaṃ ca / anena śakyakriyatvaṃ śakyajñānopādānadikatvaṃ copādhirityuktaṃ bhavati / asya vyabhicāronnāyakatvaṃ satpratipakṣonnāyakatvaṃ vā bodhyam /
evaṃ kāryatvahetorabhimatakartṛpūrvakatvāsādhakatvamuktvānabhimatāpādakatvaṃ cāha '
children.translated_text: and so forth. 'Of such a kind' means: fit to be achievable through effort, and having material cause and so forth fit to be knowable. By this, it is stated that the possibility of being made and the possibility of having knowable material cause and so forth constitute the limiting condition. This should be understood as indicating deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) or the presence of a counter-reason (<s>satpratipakṣa</s>). Having thus stated the incapacity of the effect-nature reason to establish the intended maker, he also states its establishing what is unintended, beginning with
'Moreover'

children.text: 'ti / sapakṣe hi ghaṭādau vigrahavattvasvārthāpekṣatvānīśvaratvādiviśiṣṭakartṛpūrvakatvena kāryatvasya vyāptirgṛhītā / viśiṣṭasādhyena gṛhītavyāptikaṃ ca śarīrādi viśiṣṭameva kartāraṃ sādhayet pakṣe /te cākārā abhimataviparītā iti viruddhavyāpyatvāddhetorviruddhatvamiti bhāvaḥ / nanvevaṃ sapakṣe mahānasādau kārīṣatvādimatā vahninā gṛhītavyāptinā dhūmena pakṣe parvate kārīṣādivahnereva sādhanaṃ syāt / sa ca tatra nāstīti aprāmāṇyaprasaṅgo 'numānamātrasyetyatrāha '
children.translated_text: and so forth. For in the similar instance (<s>sapakṣa</s>) — pots and the like — the pervasion of effect-nature with being preceded by a maker qualified by embodiment, desire for self-interest, non-lordship, and so forth has been grasped. And a reason whose pervasion has been grasped with a qualified probandum would establish in the thesis-subject only a similarly qualified maker. And those qualifications are the opposite of what is intended — hence the reason is contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>) due to being pervaded by what contradicts [the intended probandum]. This is the purport. Objection: If so, then by smoke — whose pervasion with fire qualified by cow-dung and the like has been grasped in the similar instance of a kitchen — only cow-dung fire and the like would be established in the thesis-subject of a mountain. And since that [cow-dung fire] is not present there, there would be the absurd consequence of the invalidity of all inference. To this he responds, beginning with
'Not so'
and so forth.
'Another <s>pramāṇa</s>'

children.text:
