'ti / sādhyasya pramāṇāntaragrahyatve liṅgabalātprasaktānāṃ viruddhaviśeṣāṇāṃ pratyakṣādināpavadanāt vahnimātre prāmāṇyamanumānasyavyavasthāpyaṃ bhavennāma / pramāṇāntarāgocare tu sādhye liṅgabalaprasaktānāṃ viparītaviśeṣāṇāmapavādakābhāvāttathaivāvasthānaṃ syādityāśayaḥ /
anvayavyatirekasahacāragrahādyadyaddharmāvacchinnakartṛpūrvatvena kāryatvasya vyāptirgṛhītā, te kulālādyanugatā anīśvatvasaṃsāritvādayo bhavanti vyāpakatāvacchedakatvena gṛhītāḥ /
vyāpakatāvacchedakadharmaprakāreṇa sādhyānumāpakatvasvābhāvyācca liṅgasyānīśvarasaṃsārikartṛmātraparyavasāyitvaṃ kāryatvahetukasakartṛkatvānumānasyeti '
children.translated_text: and so forth. When the probandum is graspable by another <s>pramāṇa</s>, the contrary particulars that threaten to arise from the force of the mark are set aside by perception and so forth, and so the inference can be established as valid for fire in general alone. But when the probandum is not within the range of another <s>pramāṇa</s>, since there is no means to set aside the contrary particulars arising from the force of the mark, they would remain as they are. This is the intent. From the apprehension of positive and negative concomitance, the pervasion of effect-nature with being preceded by a maker delimited by whatever properties — those properties, following potters and the like, turn out to be non-lordship, being a <s>saṃsārin</s> (transmigrating being), and so forth, grasped as the delimiting property of the pervader. And because of the natural tendency of the mark to lead to the inference of the probandum in the mode of the delimiting property of the pervader, the inference of having a maker from the reason of effect-nature terminates in a merely non-divine, transmigrating maker. This is what is intended by
'Whatever'

children.text:
' ityādinā vivakṣitam /
īśvarasya jatkartṛtvāsaṃbhavādapi niruktānumānamanīśvara eva viśrāmyatītyabhiprayannāha '
children.translated_text: and so forth. Also because the creatorship of <s>Īśvara</s> is impossible, the stated inference comes to rest in a non-divine [agent] alone — intending this, he says
'Moreover'

children.text: ' ti / svārthaḥ-svaprayojanam / kāruṇyam-paraprayojanasampādanopayogiguṇaviśeṣaḥ parārthaparyayavannaḥ / svārthecchāyāḥ kāruṇyasya vā sattayā vyāpyaṃ buddimatpravṛttisāmānyamiti pūrvārdhasyārthaḥ / siṣādhayiṣitasyeśvarasya tvavāptakāmatvānna svārthaḥ sādhanīyaḥ kaścana sambhavati sṛṣṭihetuḥ,na vā kāruṇyam, paraduḥkhadarśanādhīnoddhodhatvāttasya pralaye ca pareṣāṃ duḥkhasyaivābhāvāt / ataḥsvārthābhisandhisamudbuddhakāruṇyānyatararūpavyāpakanivṛttyā jagatkaraṇarūpapravṛtternivṛttirityuttarārdhasyārthaḥ // 11 //
children.translated_text: and so forth. 'Self-interest' means 'one's own purpose.' 'Compassion (<s>kāruṇya</s>)' means a special quality useful for accomplishing another's purpose — it is synonymous with 'for the sake of others.' The meaning of the first half [of the verse] is: the general activity of a deliberate agent is pervaded by the presence of either self-interest or compassion. But for the intended <s>Īśvara</s>, since his desires are fulfilled (<s>avāptakāma</s>), there is no self-interest whatsoever that could be a possible cause of creation; nor is there compassion, since that [compassion] depends on seeing others' suffering and in dissolution there is the very absence of others' suffering. Therefore, through the cessation of the pervader — [which is] either self-interest or aroused compassion — there is the cessation of the activity in the form of creating the world. This is the meaning of the second half. // 11 //

body.translated_text: Now he states the defects in the reason of effect-nature (<s>kāryatva</s>), beginning with
If he creates the world out of compassion, he should produce nothing but happiness;
and if [he creates] in conformity with the <s>karmas</s> [of beings], his independence would be diminished. // 12 //

body.text: na copādānādisākṣātkāriṇa eva kartṛtvamityapi niyamaḥ ; upīdānamupakaraṇaṃ cāviduṣa evātmano jñanādiṣu kartṛtvāt /
body.translated_text: Moreover, there is no rule that only one who directly perceives the material cause and so forth can be a maker; for even one's own self, which does not know [its material cause], has agency with respect to cognition and so forth.

children.translated_text: 'Since desires are fulfilled'
and so forth. He states the impossibility of compassion by another method, beginning with
'Nothing but happiness'

children.text: ' ti ślokārdhena / pratyutaḥ duḥkhālayaṃ jagatsṛjato na kāruṇyaleśo 'pi ghaṭata iti bhāvaḥ / nanvīśvaraḥ kāruṇyenaiva sraṣṭuṃ pravṛttaṃ / athāpi sṛjyakarmāpekṣayā sarjanānna nairghṛṇyādiprasaṅga ityatrāha '
children.translated_text: —by the half-verse. On the contrary, not even a trace of compassion is possible for one who creates the world as an abode of suffering—this is the purport. Objection: God has undertaken to create precisely out of compassion. Or alternatively, since creation is with reference to the <s>karma</s> of those to be created, there is no undesirable consequence of cruelty—to this he says,
'That <s>karma</s>—'

children.text: ' ti / tathā sati karmapāratantryaprasaṅgādīśvaratvaṃ bhajyeteti bhāvaḥ / ūśāvaro yadi jagatkartā syādanavāptakāmatvādimān syāditi pratitarko 'trānusandheyaḥ / pratiprayogastvagre vakṣyata eva // 12 //
children.translated_text: That being so, the purport is that God's lordship would be compromised due to the undesirable consequence of dependence on <s>karma</s>. The counter-argument to be considered here is: if God were the creator of the world, He would possess unfulfilled desires and the like. The counter-formulation will be stated later. || 12 ||

body.translated_text: He elaborates the meaning of the verse itself beginning with
Therefore—due to unestablishedness, contradictoriness, and the described inconclusiveness,
the creatorship of the world as stated above does not follow from the reason of effect-nature (<s>kāryatva</s>). || 13 ||

children.text: prayogaśca bhavati-mahīmahīdharādi kāryaṃna bhavati, prasiddhakāryavilakṣaṇatvāt, gaganavat ; aśakyadarśanopādānopakaraṇatvādvā, vyatirekeṇa ghaṭādivat / paramāṇavona pratyakṣāḥ niratiśayasūkṣmadravyatvāt tathaiva ghaṭādivat / vimativiṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: And the formal proof is: The earth, mountains, and the like are not effects, because they are dissimilar to well-known effects, like space; or because their material cause and instruments are impossible to perceive, by negative concomitance, like pots and the like. Atoms are not perceptible, because they are substances of unsurpassable subtlety, just like pots and the like. The object of dispute—

body.text: kālo na lokaśūnyaḥ, kālatvādidānīntanakālavat / tanubhuvanādīśvarakartṛkaṃ na bhavati kāryatvāttadvadeva / īśvaraḥ kartā na bhavati prayojanarahitatvādaśarīratvādvā muktātmavaditi /
body.translated_text: time is not devoid of a world, because it is time, like present time. The body, worlds, and the like are not created by God, because they are effects, just like that [i.e., known effects created by finite agents]. God is not a creator, because He is devoid of purpose or because He is bodiless, like a liberated soul.

children.translated_text: 'Nor is [the creator who knows] the material cause and the like—'

children.text:
' ti / jñanādiviśeṣaguṇoparāgeṇaivātmanaḥ pratyakṣatvāt jñānārthapravṛttivelāyāṃ nātmano jñānopādānabhūtasvātmasākṣātkāritvaṃ niyamato 'sti / na vā tadupakaraṇādṛṣṭamana ādisākṣātkartṛtva m / jñānārtha pravṛtterjñane kartṛtvaṃ samavāyitvaṃ ca paramasti / tathā copādānādyabhijñapūrvakatvābhāvavati jñānādai kāryatvasya sattvādvyabhicāra ityarthaḥ/
nirukteśvarānumānadūṣaṇāni saṅgṛhṇāti '
children.translated_text: [the reason is inconclusive]—since the self is perceived only through the coloring of specific qualities such as knowledge, it is not necessarily the case that the self directly perceives itself as the material cause of knowledge at the time of engaging in knowing objects. Nor is there direct perception of unseen entities such as the mind and the like as instruments. The highest that can be said is that the self has agency and inherence-relation with respect to knowledge in the activity of knowing objects. And thus, since the property of being an effect exists in knowledge and the like, which lack being preceded by a creator who knows the material cause etc., there is deviation—this is the meaning. He summarizes the refutations of the inference for God as stated:
'Due to unestablishedness—'

children.text: ' diti / kāryatvasya kṣityādāvasiddhiraśakyakriyatvādinākāryatvānumānāttasya anīśvaratvānavāpta kāmatvaśarīritvādiviparītākārakṣepakatvāt kṣityādau kartuḥ siṣādhayiṣitasya kāryatvasya viruddhatvam / abhimataviparītākārākṣepakatvaṃ hetorviruddhatvamiti hi prācāṃ paribhāṣā / anaiśvaryādyāpādakatvaṃ cānaiśvaryādiviśiṣṭakartṛkatvena vyāpterghaṭādau kāryatvahetorgṛhītatvādeva / kiñcacetanajanyatvamātre sādhye 'dṛṣṭadvārā jīvajanyatvasya kāryamātre 'bhimatatvātsiddhasādhanam / tadupādānādisākṣātkartṛkartṛpūrvakatvaṃ sādhyamityurarīkāryam / tatra cānupadoktamanaikāntyaṃ sthitaṃ jñānādyantarbhāvena / evamasiddhyādidoṣaduṣṭatvātkāryatvasya tena kṣityādau upādanopakaraṇādisākṣātkartṛ kartṛpūrvakatvaṃ na sādhayituṃ śakyata ityarthaḥ // 13 //
children.translated_text: The unestablishedness of effect-nature in earth and the like is due to the inference of non-effect-nature through the impossibility of action and the like. The contradictoriness of effect-nature in proving the intended creator of earth and the like is because it entails attributes contrary to what is desired—such as non-lordship, unfulfilled desires, embodiment, and so forth. For the convention of the ancients is: contradictoriness of a reason means that it entails attributes contrary to what is intended. And the implication of non-lordship and the like is because the invariable concomitance of effect-nature with having a creator qualified by non-lordship and the like has already been grasped in the case of pots and the like. Moreover, if the thing to be proved is merely 'being produced by a conscious being,' then since the effect-nature of all effects is accepted as implying production by individual souls through the medium of <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit), it is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>). If the thing to be proved is 'being preceded by a creator who directly perceives the material cause and the like,' this must be conceded. And there the inconclusiveness stated above stands, through the inclusion of knowledge and the like. Thus, because the reason of effect-nature is vitiated by the defects of unestablishedness and the like, it cannot establish that earth and the like are preceded by a creator who directly perceives the material cause, instruments, and the like—this is the meaning. || 13 ||

body.translated_text: Now he also states the inconclusiveness in proving that [effects are] preceded by a creator who knows the material cause and the like:

body.text: atra brūmo na kāryatvaṃ kṣityādau śakyanihnavam /
body.translated_text: Here we say: The effect-nature of earth and the like cannot be denied,
because of similarity to known effects, because of possessing action, and because of being characterized by magnitude. || 14 ||
Because of corporeality of such a kind, accompanied by external perceptibility,
and because of being the substratum of generic universals—from these reasons and others, like pots and the like. || 15 ||

children.text: na cedṛśa eva sanniveśaḥ kāryaḥ netara ityavayavasanniveśaviśeṣapratiniyataṃ rūpabhedamudīkṣāmahe / yattu śakyakriyaṃ śakyajñānopādānopakaraṇaṃ ca kriyata ita, tadastu nāma / kintu te kriyājñānaśaktī kriyājñānābhyāmeva samadhigamanīye / te ca kṣityādiṣu yathoktasādhanabalasamupasthāpite iti na viśeṣaḥ
children.translated_text: And we do not look for a distinction of form invariably restricted to a specific arrangement of parts, such that only such an arrangement is an effect and nothing else. As for what is said—that it is capable of action and capable of being known through material cause and instruments—let that be so. But those two powers of action and knowledge are to be ascertained only through action and knowledge themselves. And those are established in earth and the like through the force of the aforementioned reasons—thus there is no difference

body.text: prasiddhaprākāragopurādi kāryebhyastanubhuvanādeḥ / nacaitāvāneva kriyāgocara iti viṣayaniyamaḥ kaścit kriyāya dṛṣṭaḥ ; yenedamaśakyakriyamadhyavasyema / siddhe ca kāryatve tadupādānādisākṣātkaraṇatadadhiṣṭhānatatpreraṇanipuṇaḥ puruṣaviśeṣa sidhyatyeva /
body.translated_text: between the body, worlds, and so forth, and well-known effects such as walls, gate-towers, and the like. And no restriction of the scope of action has been observed such that only this much is within the range of action and nothing more, by which we would conclude that this is incapable of being acted upon. And when effect-nature is established, a particular person skilled in the direct perception, governance, and impelling of the material cause and the like of that effect is indeed established.

body.text: adhiṣṭhānaṃ ca tatpravṛttyanuguṇasaṅkalpavadīśvarasannikarṣaḥ, kṣetrājñeneva svaśarīrādau / sa ca dravyaiḥ saṃyogalakṣaṇaḥ, tadguṇaistisaṃyuktasamavāyarūpaḥ / pravṛttiśca paramāṇūnāṃ parispandalakṣaṇā ; dharmādharmayostu phalodayānukūlatādṛśadeśakālādisahakārisahitatā / tābhyāṃ dharmādharmābhyāmeva phalam, cetanānadhiṣṭhitānāṃ sarveṣāmeteṣāmacaitanyenākiñcitkaratvāt / na hi cetanena vardhakinānadhiṣṭhitā vāsī / deśakālādisahakāri śatasamadhigame 'pi yūpādīnyāpādayitumalam / bījāṅkurādayastu pakṣāntarbhūtā iti tairvyabhicāravacanamanabhijñatayaiva śrotriyāṇām / etena sukhādibhirvyabhicāro 'pi pratyuktaḥ / na cobhayavādisiddhatāmātreṇa kṣetrajñānāmevedṛśādhiṣṭhātṛtvakalpanamucitam ; teṣāṃ sūkṣmavyavahitādidarśanā śakterniścitatvāt / dṛṣṭānusāriṇī hi sarvatra kalpanā ; na dṛṣvirodhinī / na caivamīśvarasyāśaktirniścitā ; pramāṇāntaratasta(da)tsiddheḥ / yathoditapramāṇabalena sidhyam sāṃsiddhikasarvārthadarśanatatpreraṇaśaktisampanna eva sidhyati ; kāryatvasya samarthakartṛpūrvakatvena pratibandhāt /
body.translated_text: And the governance is the proximity of <s>Īśvara</s> (God) possessing volition conforming to the activity of that creation, just as the individual soul (<s>kṣetrajña</s>) governs its own body and so forth. And that proximity is of the nature of conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) with substances, and with their qualities it takes the form of conjoined-inherence (<s>saṃyuktasamavāya</s>). And the activity of atoms is characterized by vibration; but for <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit), it is the possession of cooperating conditions of such-and-such place, time, and the like, favorable to the arising of fruit. It is by those two—<s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> alone—that fruit comes, since all these material factors, not being governed by a conscious being, are powerless due to their non-consciousness. For indeed, an adze not governed by a conscious carpenter, even with a hundred cooperating conditions of place, time, and the like being obtained, is not sufficient to produce sacrificial posts and the like. As for seeds, sprouts, and the like—they fall within the thesis to be proved, and so citing them as counter-examples is merely the ignorance of the orthodox. By this, the counter-example of pleasure and the like is also answered. And it is not appropriate to imagine that individual souls (<s>kṣetrajña</s>) alone possess such governance merely because it is accepted by both parties, for their incapacity to perceive subtle, obstructed, and similar objects has been ascertained. For inference everywhere follows what is observed, not what contradicts observation. And God's incapacity has not been ascertained in this way, because His capacity is established through other means of knowledge. What is established by the force of the stated means of proof is established as precisely one endowed with innate powers of perceiving all objects and impelling them, because effect-nature is invariably concomitant with being preceded by a competent creator.

children.text: yattu parimitaśaktijñānānaiśvaryādyāpadanāddharmaviśeṣaviparīsādhanatva mudbhāvitam, tadatisthadhīyaḥ, aprayojakatvātteṣam / na hi kiñcit kriyamāṇaṃ karturarthāntaraviṣayamasāmarthyamajñānāṃ vā svotpatte 'pekṣate ; svasabhpādanasamarthakartṛmātrākṣepāt kevalavyatirekāsiddheḥ / tāvataivopapadyamāne kāryodaye sambandino 'kiñcitkarasyārthāntaraviṣayasyābhāvasya hetutva kalpanānupapatteḥ / api ca kiṃ taditaramastavastuvi, yamajñānādi vyāpakam, uta katipayagocaramiti vivecanīyam / na tāvadaśeṣaviṣayam, anupalabdheḥ / na khalu kumbhakāraḥ kumbhātireki kimapi na vijānāti / atha katipayaviṣayam / tadapi na, aniyataviṣayatayā tasya tasyavyabhicāradarśanāt / na cāstikiñcidvyavasthitam,
children.translated_text: As for what has been raised—that the reason establishes the opposite of what is intended by entailing limited power, knowledge, non-lordship, and the like—that is the thinking of the dull-witted, because those attributes are non-productive of the effect. For nothing that is being produced requires the incapacity or ignorance of its maker regarding other objects; because the reason merely implies a maker capable of producing the thing in question, and the negative concomitance alone remains unestablished. Since, when the arising of the effect is explained by just those capabilities, it is unreasonable to posit the absence—which is causally irrelevant and pertains to other objects—as a reason for the effect. Moreover, one should examine: Is that ignorance and the like regarding other things all-pervading in scope, or pertaining to only some objects? It is certainly not all-pervading, because it is not observed. For a potter is not ignorant of everything other than pots. If pertaining to some objects—that too is untenable, because of the observation of its deviation due to its having no fixed domain of objects. And there is nothing fixed

body.translated_text: such that only one who possesses ignorance and the like experiences creatorship.

body.text: na ca śarīriṇaiva kartrā bhāvyam, śarīragrahaṇenaivānaikāntyāt / na khalu śarīraviśiṣṭassannevāyamātmā śarīramupādatte, ayoginoyugapadanekaśarīra grahaṇāyogāt/pūrvadhaparityāgena dehāntaraprāpakakarmapreritaprāṇasahāya eva dehāntaraṃ praviśatītyupapāditamātmacintāyām/
body.translated_text: And it is not the case that only an embodied being can be a creator, because the very mention of 'body' renders the reason inconclusive. For this self does not take up a body while already possessing a body in the same life, since for one who is not a <s>yogin</s>, it is impossible to simultaneously possess multiple bodies. It has been established in the <s>Ātmacintā</s> that the self, having abandoned the previous body, enters another body assisted by the vital breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) impelled by <s>karma</s> that leads to another body.

body.text: kiñcātmanaḥ śarīramadhitiṣṭhato 'dhiṣṭhānakriyātakarmabhūtasya dehasyādhiṣṭhātṛdaśā (dehā)nupraveśo 'nupapannaḥ, yugapadekakriyāyāmekasya karmakartṛtvavirodhāt / adhitiṣṭhāsitadehasaṃyogavata eva tatpravṛttyanuguṇa prayatnayogalakṣaṇamadhiṣṭhānaṃ dṛṣṭamiti cet ; astvekatattva (satva)sambaddhasyādhiṣṭhānānupapatteḥ preryavastusambhandhinā prerakeṇa bhavitavyamiti ; na punardehasambandhena (ndhinā) bhāvyamiti / kuto nirṇayaḥ ? ita eva, yato 'nyadapyadhiṣṭhīyamānaṃ mānajaṇḍādi svasambandhinauvādhiṣṭhīyate / tenādhiṣṭhānakriyāpekṣitādhiṣṭheyapadārthasambhandhamātrātirekeṇa dehasambandho nāmaparo nādartavyaḥ asti ceśvarasyāpi jagadupādānopakaraṇaissambandha ityuktameva /
body.translated_text: Moreover, for the self that governs the body—the body being the object of the governance-action—entry into the body in the condition of a governor is untenable, because of the contradiction in one entity being simultaneously the object and agent of a single action. If it be said that governance, characterized by the conjunction of effort conforming to the activity of the body one intends to govern, has been observed—so be it; but since governance cannot be established for one who is connected with that very entity to be governed, the governor must be connected with the entity to be governed as something distinct from himself. But it need not be said that the governor must be connected through a body-connection. Whence this determination? From this very fact: that other things being governed, such as carriages, palanquins, and the like, are governed only by one connected to them, not necessarily through a body. Therefore, beyond the mere connection with the object to be governed that is required for the action of governance, no additional body-connection need be regarded. And <s>Īśvara</s> too has a connection with the material cause and instruments of the world—this has already been stated.

body.text: atha svadehavyatirikta vastuni pravṛttiviśeṣakaratvaṃ dehadvāreṇaiva / dṛṣṭaṃ hi daṇḍacakrādiṣu karasaṃyogādinā kulālādeḥ pravartayitṛtvamityucyeta ; tadapi na ; abhidhyānamātreṇaiva paraśarīragatagaranirasanavisāraṇadarśanāt /
body.translated_text: Now, if it be said that the capacity to set in motion things other than one's own body is only through the medium of the body—for it is observed that the potter's capacity to set in motion a staff, wheel, and the like is through the conjunction of the hand and so forth—that too is untenable; because it is observed that by mere mental intention (<s>abhidhyāna</s>), the dispelling and spreading of poison residing in another's body can occur.

body.text: kathamasati śarīre parapreraṇātmakaḥ saṅkalpa iti cet ; kiṃ śarīraṃ saṅkalpayati, yena tadabhāve na bhavet ? / karaṇamiti cenna; manasaḥ karaṇatvāt kimastīśvarasya manaḥ ? bāḍham / nanvevaṃ vugrahadharmādharmānaiśvaryādayaḥ sādhāraṇadharmāḥ prāduḥṣyuḥ / maivam ; kāryatvākṣiptasamarthakartṛmattvāt (ttvārtha) draḍhimnaivāpāstatvāt / manaso nityendriyatayā dehāpagame 'pi sambandhābhyupagamādanaikāntikaśca / yāvaddhi dṛṣṭānuguṇaṃ vyāptyupayogi, tāvadanujñāyate / nacāsmadādermanasāpyacintyaracanasyāparyantavistārasya mahābhūtabhautikaprapañcasya prādeśikaśarīrakaḥ kiñcijjñaḥ puṇyapāpaparavaśagatiralaṃ nirmāṇāyetyaparimitajñānaiśvaryaśaktiḥ śarīrādyanapekṣaḥ saṅkalpādeva sakalabhuvananirmāṇakṣamaḥ kartā siddhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Objection: How can there be volition (<s>saṅkalpa</s>), which is of the nature of directing others, in the absence of a body? [Reply:] Does the body will? — that without it there would be no [willing]? If [you say] 'it is the instrument' — no; for the mind is the instrument. Does <s>Īśvara</s> (God) have a mind? Certainly. Objection: If so, then common properties such as merit, demerit, non-sovereignty, and so forth would arise. Not so; because these are already dispelled by the very firmness [of the conclusion] that [the world] must have a capable maker, as required by its being an effect. And since the mind, being an eternal sense-faculty, is accepted as connected [with the self] even in the absence of a body, [the objection] is also inconclusive. For only so much as is conducive to the establishment of pervasion in accordance with what is observed is accepted. And it is not the case that someone like us — a limited knower, embodied in a provincial body, whose course is governed by merit and demerit — is capable of constructing the vast expanse of the material and physical manifold, whose marvelous construction is inconceivable even to the mind. Therefore, a maker of unlimited knowledge, sovereignty, and power, independent of body and so forth, capable of constructing the entire universe by volition alone, is established.

children.text: īdṛśena kartrā ghaṭādiṣu kāryatvasya sambandho na dṛṣṭa iti cet ;
children.translated_text: Objection: The connection of 'being an effect' (<s>kāryatva</s>) with such a maker has not been observed in [cases like] pots and the like.

body.text: atigahanagiritaṭādhiṣṭhānenātiprakṛṣṭādṛṣṭacarendhananivahasambandhinā hutavahaviśeṣeṇa mahānasādau dhūmasya vā kiṃ sambandho dṛṣṭaḥ ? yena dhūmaviśeṣadarśanāt giriśikhare tathāvidhāgniranumīyate / yādṛśo dhūmo yatrāvagataḥ tatraiva tādṛśastatsampādanasamarthau dṛṣṭāntabhūmāvaparidṛṣṭo 'pi sāmānyavyāptibalena pakṣadhramatāvaśāt sidhyatītita cet ; tadidamasmābhirabhidhīyamānaṃ kimiti na hṛdayamadhihohati bhavatām / imāpi kāryatvaṃ samarthakartṛpūrvakatvena ghaṭādiṣu viditasambandhaniyamaṃ kṣityādiṣu dṛśyamānaṃ svasampādanasamarthamadṛṣṭapūrvameva buddhimatkartāramupasthāpayati / yathaiva hi deśakālendhanaparimāṇādiviśeṣānādareṇa dhūmasya svodayānuguṇahutavahamātreṇa sambndhaniyamaḥ,tathaivānīśvaratvākiñcijjñatvaśarīritvapuṇyapāpaparavaśatvamanuṣyatvādi- viśeṣaprahāṇena kāryasya svinirmāṇasamarkhabuddhimatkartṛmātreṇa sambandhaniyamaniścaya iti na kaścidviśeṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: [Reply:] Has the connection of smoke in a kitchen with a particular fire associated with a mass of unseen fuel, located on an extremely remote, dense mountain slope, been observed? — by which, from seeing a particular smoke on a mountain peak, such a fire is inferred? If [you say]: Whatever type of smoke was observed wherever — even though the fire capable of producing it, in exactly that form, has not been observed in the domain of the example, still, by the force of general pervasion, it is established due to the necessity of its being present in the thesis — if so, then this very thing that we are saying, why does it not enter your hearts? This 'being an effect,' too, having its connection-rule with 'being preceded by a capable maker' known in [cases like] pots and the like, when observed in earth and the like, presents a previously-unseen intelligent maker capable of producing it. For just as the connection-rule of smoke with merely a fire suited to its own arising [holds] regardless of the particular differences of place, time, quantity of fuel, and so forth — in exactly the same way, there is the determinate connection-rule of an effect with merely an intelligent maker capable of its own construction, abandoning the particular [limitations of] non-sovereignty, limited-knowledge, embodiedness, subjection to merit and demerit, humanity, and so forth. There is no difference [between the two cases].

body.text: api ca vibhudravyasaṃyoginaḥ parispandavataśca sarvatra sparśavattvāvyābhicāre 'pi jñānasukhādinityadravyaviśeṣaguṇānumitātmasaṃyogino manasaḥ kathamiva sparśarahitatvam ? kathaṃ na vāyavīyadravyasyamahimaguṇaśālino niyatādhiṣṭhānaspārśanatvaniyamadarśane 'pi tvagindriye tadviparyayaḥ ? taijasasya vā rūpasparśayoranyattarasya vā prākaṭyaniyame 'pi rūpopalambhasādhanatānumitataijasabhāsya cakṣuṣo niyamena tadubhayānudbhavābhyupagamaḥ ? / atha kāryadarśanānumitasadbhāvānāṃ taijasādibhāve 'pi tattadviśeṣāṇāṃ yogyānupalabdhibādhitatvāt tadabhyupagame 'nekaniyamabhaṅgaprasaṅgācca tathābhyupagamaḥ, hanta tarhi prakṛviṣaye 'pi prasaḍhañjitadharmaviśeṣāṇāmanupalambhabādhāviśeṣāt anekaniyamadarśanavighātaprasaṅgācca tathābhyupagama iti sarvaṃ samānamanyatrābhiniveśāt /
body.translated_text: Moreover, how is the mind — which is conjoined with the self inferred through the special qualities of eternal substances such as knowledge and pleasure, and which is conjoined with all-pervading substances and possessing motion — devoid of touch, when there is no deviation from tangibility everywhere [for such substances]? And how is there a reversal for the skin-organ regarding the wind-substance, which possesses the quality of greatness and whose contact with a fixed substrate is observed to be regular? Or how is there the acceptance of the definite non-arising of both [color and touch] for the eye — whose fiery nature is inferred by its being the instrument for perceiving color — when, for a fiery substance, there is a rule that either color or touch [at least one] is manifest? If [one says]: although the fiery and other natures of things whose existence is inferred from observing effects [might hold], since the particular [properties] in each case are refuted by qualified non-apprehension, and since accepting [them] would entail the breaking of many established rules — therefore such acceptance [is justified]; well then, in the present case too, since there is no difference in the refutation by non-apprehension of particular properties that are established for the simple [class], and since there would equally be the consequence of breaking many observed rules — therefore the same acceptance [should hold]. Everything is the same, except for [your] bias.

body.text: dṛśyante hi nītayaḥ / yathā-vivādāspadaṃ paramāṇvādi prekṣāvapreritaṃ ceṣṭate, acetanatvāt ; yadacetanaṃ tattathā, yathā tathāvidhaṃ kandukādi / tathā vivādādhyāsitā bāhyābhyantarapravṛttaya-prakṛtyupakaraṇapratyakṣapūrvikāḥ kāryatvāttadvadeva /
body.translated_text: For such logical procedures are observed: For example — the entity in dispute, namely atoms and the like, moves as impelled by one possessed of foresight, because it is non-conscious; whatever is non-conscious is so, like a ball of that type. Likewise, the external and internal activities that are the seat of the dispute are preceded by direct perception of the material cause and instruments, because of being effects — just like [pots and the like].

children.translated_text: 'And the formal proof'
— thus. He adduces the fact that the material cause is incapable of being perceived:
'Atoms'

children.text:
'
iti / tathaiva-vyatirekeṇaiva / kāryatvasya pakṣe kṣityādau asiddhisādhanāya prayoga uktaḥ / atha jīvaiḥ siddhasādhanatvasādhanārtha pralayanirāse prayoga ucyate '
children.translated_text: — thus. 'In exactly that way' means: by negative concomitance alone. A formal proof has been stated to establish the non-establishment [of the reason] 'being an effect' in the thesis, namely earth and the like. Now, a formal proof is stated for the purpose of establishing that [the conclusion] is already-established by <s>jīvas</s>, through the refutation of dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>):
'The subject of dispute'

children.text: ' ti / sati hi pralaye sargārambhesraṣṭṛtvaṃ jīvānāṃ karaṇādividhuratvānna ghaṭata iti kartrantaraṃ mantavyaṃ bhavet / tat sarvakāryadravyavirahalakṣaṇaḥ pralayo nāstyeveti sādhyate 'tra / viruddhatvapradarśanārthaḥ prayogaḥ '
children.translated_text: — thus. For if there were dissolution, then at the beginning of creation, the creatorship of <s>jīvas</s> would not be possible due to their being bereft of instruments [of knowledge] — therefore another creator would have to be accepted. Hence, the total dissolution of all effect-substances does not exist at all — this is what is proved here. The formal proof for showing the contradictory [conclusion] is:
'The body, universe, and so forth'

children.text: ' ti / īśvarakartṛkaṃ na bhavatītyanīśvarakartṛkaṃ bhavatītyarthaparyavasāyi / tadvadeva-anvayena ghaṭādivadeva / viparītaparyavasāyitvaṃ kāryatvānumānasyoktam / abhimataparyavasāyitvābhāvaṃ ca sphorayati '
children.translated_text: — thus. '[The world] is not made by <s>Īśvara</s>' has the implication 'it is made by a non-<s>Īśvara</s>.' 'Just like that' means: by positive concomitance, just like a pot and the like. The contrary implication of the inference from 'being an effect' has been stated. And he makes explicit the absence of the desired implication:
'<s>Īśvara</s>'

children.text:
' iti / īśvaraḥīśvaratvābhimataḥ / ayaṃ ca satpratipakṣarūpaḥ /
evaṃ mīmāṃsakaidrūṣitameveśvarānumānaṃ tārkikaprakriyāmevāvalambya prāyaśo vyavaśthāpayitumupakramate doṣoddhāramukhena '
children.translated_text: — thus. '<s>Īśvara</s>' means one who claims to be <s>Īśvara</s>. And this [counter-argument] is in the form of a genuine counter-proof (<s>satpratipakṣa</s>). Thus, relying mostly on the very procedure of the logicians (<s>Tārkikas</s>), he begins to establish the inference of <s>Īśvara</s> that has been refuted by the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>, through the method of removing the defects:
'Here we say'

children.text: 'ityādinā / kāryatvam-utpattimattvam / kṣityādeḥ kāryatve hetavaḥ sabhāgatvādayaḥ / sabhāgatvaṃ-sāvayavatvam / '
children.translated_text: — with this and what follows. 'Being an effect' means: having origination. The reasons for earth and the like being effects are: being composite (<s>sabhāgatva</s>) and so forth. 'Being composite' means having parts.
'From earth and the like'

children.text: 'iti pracīnamudritapāṭhastu na samīcīnaḥ / kriyāvattvaṃ, paricchinnaparimāṇavattvarūpaṃ mūrtatvaṃ ca nityaparamāṇusādhāraṇamiti sāmānādhikaraṇyasambandhena mahattvaviśiṣṭaṃ taddetūkṛtam / sāmānyaviśeṣaḥ-dravyatvādi pṛthitvādi ca, tacac kevalaṃ nityaparamāṇvādisādhāraṇamiti bāhyapratyakṣaviṣayatvena viśeṣitaṃ taddhetūkṛtam / ātmano mānasapratyakṣatvātsāmānyaviśeṣavattvācca tatra vyabhicāra iti bāhyatvena pratyakṣaṃ viśeṣitam // 14 // 15 //
children.translated_text: — thus; but the reading of the older printed edition is not correct. 'Possessing activity,' 'possessing delimited dimension' — i.e., 'being material' (<s>mūrtatva</s>) — [these properties] are common to eternal atoms as well; therefore, they are made into reasons as qualified by 'greatness' through the relation of co-referentiality. 'Universal-and-particular' means <s>dravyatva</s> (substancehood), <s>pṛthivītva</s> (earthness), and so forth — these too, being common to eternal atoms and the like, are made into reasons as qualified by 'being the object of external perception.' Since the self (<s>ātman</s>) is an object of mental perception and possesses universal-and-particular, there would be deviation; hence [the reason is] qualified by 'external' perception. // 14 // 15 //

body.translated_text: He states the counter-proofs:
That [earth and the like] is perceptible, because of being a knowable object (<s>prameya</s>), because of being a category (<s>padārtha</s>), like a pot and the like.
This [world] conforms to a single will, because of being non-conscious, like one's own body. // 16 //

body.text: nanu kāryatvamastu niruktahetubhiḥ / tāvatā sakartṛkatve kimāyātam ? kāryasāmānye kartuḥ kāraṇatve mānābhāvāt, kartāṃ vināpi kāraṇāntarata eva kṣityāderutpattisambhavādityatrāha '

children.translated_text: 'Not such'

children.text:
' iti / sāvayavatvaṃ hyavayavasanniveśaviśeṣarūpākṛtimattvam / tacca puruśakṛtisādhyameva dṛṣṭamiti vicitrākārasya mahyaderapi sakartṛkatvameṣṭavyameva / kāryaviśeṣatvameva sakartṛkatvavyāpyamastu / sa ca viśeṣo na kṣoṇyādivyāvṛtta iti tasyāpi sakartṛkatvasiddhirapratihatā / kiñca 'yadviśeṣayo'rityādinyāyena kāryaviśeṣo kulālādeḥ kāraṇatvāt kāryatvāvacchinne 'pi
kartṛtvāvacchinnasya kāraṇatvamastyeveti kāryatvameva sakartṛkatvavyāpyaṃ kṣityādau kartāraṃsamarthayatīti bhāvaḥ / yadvā kṣityādi na kāryaṃ prasiddhakāryavilakṣaṇatvādityatrāprayojakatvamāha '
children.translated_text: — thus. For 'being composite' (<s>sāvayavatva</s>) is [by definition] 'having a particular configuration of parts' — i.e., 'having a form' (<s>ākṛtimatva</s>). And that is observed as achievable only through human effort (<s>puruṣakṛti</s>). Therefore, the earth and the like, having variegated forms, must also be accepted as having a maker. Let 'being a particular effect' alone be what is pervaded by 'having a maker.' And that particularity is not excluded from earth and the like. Therefore, the establishment of their having a maker is unobstructed. Moreover, by the principle 'whatever [is the cause] of a particular [effect]' and so forth, since the particular effect has the potter and the like as its cause — even in [effectness] delimited by 'being an effect,' there is indeed causality delimited by 'having a maker' — therefore, 'being an effect' itself, being pervaded by 'having a maker,' establishes a maker for earth and the like — this is the purport. Alternatively, [against the objection that] earth and the like are not effects because they are different from well-known effects, he states the non-applicability [of this]:
'Not such'

children.text: ' iti/ kāryaḥ-kṛtijanyaḥ, utpattimān vā / kṛtijanyatve vā prayojakaṃ kṣoṇyādyākāravyāvṛttaṅghaṭādyākāramātravṛttidharmaviśeṣaṃ na paśyāma ityarthaḥ / sati hi tasmin viśeṣe prasiddhakāryavailakṣaṇyasyākartṛkartṛkatvavyāptiḥ prasidhyet / anyathā tvaprayojakatvameva adṛṣṭakartṛko rājaprāsādo na kāryo daṣṭakartṛkaghaṭādikāryavilakṣaṇatvādityādivaditi bhāvaḥ / nanu śakyakriyatvādireva tādṛśoviśeṣaḥ kṣityādyākṛtivyāvṛtta iti cettatrāha '
children.translated_text: — thus. 'Effect' means: produced by effort (<s>kṛti</s>), or having origination. [Against the view that] the specific property restricted only to the form of pots and the like, to the exclusion of the form of earth and the like, which would be the differentiator [between effects] produced by effort — we do not see [such a property], is the meaning. For if such a specific [differentiating] property existed, then the difference of well-known effects [from earth] might establish the pervasion with 'not having a maker.' But otherwise, the [argument from difference] is simply inapplicable — just as [one cannot argue]: 'A royal palace whose maker has not been seen is not an effect, because it is different from effects with observed makers like pots' — this is the purport. Objection: But 'being achievable through action' and the like is precisely such a specific property, excluded from the form of earth and the like. To this he says:
'But that which'
— thus.
'Let that be so'

children.text: ' ti / kṣityādau tādṛśaviśeṣābhāvo 'siddha iti hārdam / te-kriyājñāne / '
children.translated_text: — thus. The real intent is: the absence of such a specific property in earth and the like is unestablished. 'Those' — means action and knowledge.
'As stated'

children.text: 'ti kāryatvahetukasakartṛkatvānumānalakṣaṇeti yāvat / ayaṃ bhāvaḥ - upādānādigocarāparokṣajñānacikīrṣākṛtimajjanyatvaṃ hi sādhyeta mahyādau / tatra ca tadvidheyakakṛtiḥ, tadupādānādyaparokṣajñānaṃ ca ghaṭakamastyeva / jñānakriyayorevaṃ prāmāṇikatvaṃ tadanuguṇasāmarthyamapi kalpanīyameva jagatkarturityaśakyakriyatvāderasiddhiriti bhāvaḥ / kriyāgocara-kṛtividheyaḥ / '
children.translated_text: — thus, i.e., as characterized by the inference of having a maker from the reason of 'being an effect.' This is the purport: what would be proved for the earth and the like is: being produced by an effort that presupposes direct knowledge of the material cause and so forth, and volition. And therein, the effort directed by that [knowledge] and the direct knowledge of the material cause and so forth do indeed serve as [necessary] components. Since the evidential validity of both knowledge and action [as components of making] is established, the corresponding capability too must be postulated for the world-creator — therefore, [the objection of] non-establishment of 'being achievable through action' and so forth [fails] — this is the purport. 'Object of action' means: governed by effort.
'Established'

children.text:
' iti / prāmāṇike ca kāryatve sati kāryatvasya viśiṣṭakartṛpūkatvavyāptibalāt kṣityādau kartṛviśeṣasiddhirapratyūhaiveti bhāvaḥ / 'tadadhiṣṭhānatapreraṇe' ti karmadhārayaḥ / yadvā parapravṛttyanuguṇavyāpāraḥ / preramam / tādṛśavyāpāravataḥ preryeṇa sannikarṣo 'dhiṣṭhānamiti bhidā / evaṃ kāryatvaṃ kṣityādestataḥ sakartṛkatvaṃ ca sādhitam /
atha sakartṛkatvānumānasya jīvaiḥ siddhasādhanatāṃ parihartuṃ kartṛtvesvarūpānupraviṣṭamadhiṣṭānādi vivṛṇoti '
children.translated_text:
— thus. And when the effectness [of earth etc.] is established by valid means of knowledge, by the force of the invariable concomitance of effectness with having a specific maker, the establishment of a specific maker for earth and the rest is entirely unobstructed — such is the purport. '<s>tadadhiṣṭhānatapreraṇe</s>' is a <s>karmadhāraya</s> (appositional compound). Alternatively, activity that is conducive to another's operation is '<s>preraṇam</s>' (impelling). The contact of the impeller — one possessing such activity — with the impelled is '<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>' (supervision) — this is the distinction. Thus, the effectness of earth and the rest, and consequently their having a maker, has been established.
Now, in order to remove the objection of <s>siddhasādhana</s> (proving what is already established) against the inference of having a maker — [the objection being that it is] already established through <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) — he elucidates supervision and the rest as intrinsically included in the nature of agency:
'Supervision'

children.text: ' mityādinā / yathā jīvasya śarīrāvayavādyadhiṣṭānaṃ tatpravṛttyanukūlasaṅkalpena, evaṃ paramāṇyadṛṣṭādyadhiṣṭhānaṃ jagatkartṛrīśvarasya tatpravṛttyunukūlasaṅkalpeneti mantavyamityarthaḥ / '
children.translated_text: — and so forth. Just as the <s>jīva</s>'s (individual soul's) supervision of bodily parts and the like is through a volition conducive to their activity, so too, the supervision of atoms, <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit), and the rest by <s>Īśvara</s> (God), the maker of the world, should be understood as being through a volition conducive to their activity — this is the meaning.
'He'
'if'

children.text: 'ti / īśvarasannikarṣaḥ paramāṇvādau saṃyogarūpaḥ adṛṣṭe ca saṃyuktasamavāyarūpo vibhuddhayasaṃyogasyopagame / tadanupagame saṃyuktasaṃyogisamavāyalakṣaṇo bodhyaḥ /idaṃ ca tārkikaprakriyayā / '
children.translated_text: — thus. <s>Īśvara</s>'s contact with atoms and the like is in the form of conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>); and with <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit) it is in the form of <s>saṃyuktasamavāya</s> (inherence in what is conjoined), if the conjunction of an omnipresent being is accepted. If that is not accepted, it should be understood as having the character of <s>saṃyuktasaṃyogisamavāya</s> (inherence in what is conjoined with the conjoined). And this follows the Naiyāyika procedure.
'Activity'

children.text: ' riti / ārambhakasaṃyogānukūlakriyārūpā ca paramāṇūnāṃ pravṛttirityarthaḥ / adṛṣṭasya pravṛttiṃ nirvakti '
children.translated_text: — thus. The activity of the atoms means action in the form of activity conducive to the originating conjunction — this is the meaning. He explains the activity of <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit):
'Of <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit)'

children.text:
riti/ idaṃ puṇyaṃ pāpaṃ vāsmin deśe kāle ca phalaṃ janayatvitīśvarasaṅkalpamūlādṛṣṭasya pravṛttiḥ
phalodayānukūlatādṛśadeśakālādisahakārisamāsādanalakṣaṇā bhavatītyarthaḥ / '
children.translated_text: — thus. The activity of <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit), which is rooted in <s>Īśvara</s>'s volition that 'this merit or sin shall produce its fruit in such-and-such a place and time,' consists in the obtaining of the appropriate cooperating conditions such as place, time, and the rest that are conducive to the fruition of the result — this is the meaning.
'By those two'

children.text: ' miti/ evakāro bhinnakramaḥ / tābhyāṃ-cetanādhiṣṭhitābhyāmeva dharmādharmābhyāṃ palamityānvayaḥ / nanu kartāramantaraiva kāraṇāntarataḥ kṣityādi bhavediti śaṅkāmantarnidhāya tatparihāramāha '
children.translated_text: — thus. The word 'eva' (alone) is displaced in order. The construction is: fruit arises from those two — <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit) — only when they are supervised by a conscious being. Now, anticipating the objection that earth and the rest might arise from other causes without a maker at all, he states the reply to that:
'Conscious'
— thus. He establishes precisely their inefficacy [without a conscious supervisor]:
'For not'

children.text: ' ti / tathā cādhiṣṭhātuḥ kārakacakraprayoktaḥ kartṛścetanasyāpekṣā kāryasāmānye 'syeveti kṣityādau sakartṛkatvaṃ nāpahnavārham / acetanasya kāraṇagrāmasya catanādhiṣṭhānamantarā pravṛttyanupapatteriti bhāvaḥ / upādānadigocarāparokṣajñānamantarā ca tadadhiṣṭhānalakṣaṇasya kartṛtvasyāsambhavāt kṣityādikartṛḥ paramāṇvādisākṣātkāro 'pyāvaśyakaḥ / cikīrṣāpūrvakārakacakrapravṛttihetukṛtinirūpyaṃ ca preraṇamiti kārakacakraprayoktṛtvarūpādhiṣṭhātṛtvalakṣaṇasyopādānādigocarāparokṣajñānacikīrṣākṛtimattvalakṣaṇasya ca kartṛtvasya nātyantabhedaḥ / tataśca pūrvatropādānādigocarāparokṣajñānacikīrṣākṛtimattvaṃ kartṛtvamuktam / atrādhiṣṭhātṛtvarūpaṃ tat samarthyata iti parakṛtāsāṅgatyamiti śaṅkāyā nāvasara ityavadheyama / evaṃbhūtasya kṣityādikartṛtvasya sadā sarvadarśinaṃ sarvasamarthaṃ ceśvaraṃ vinānyatra jīveṣvasambhavānna taiḥ siddhasādhanamiti cātra vivakṣitam / na cobhayavādī' tyagrimagranthe caitadvakṣyate / madhye 'naikāntyaṃ paraharati prasaṃṅgataḥ '
children.translated_text: — thus. And therefore, the necessity of a conscious agent — the superintendent, the director of the assemblage of causal factors, the maker — for effects in general is such that the having-a-maker of earth and the rest is not to be denied. The purport is: because the activity of the unconscious aggregate of causes is impossible without the supervision of a conscious being. And since agency in the form of supervising those [causes] is impossible without direct perception of the material cause and the rest, the maker of earth and the rest must also necessarily have direct perception (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>) of the atoms and the rest. And since impelling is defined as the exertion that causes the operation of the assemblage of causal factors preceded by the desire to act (<s>cikīrṣā</s>), there is no absolute difference between agency in the form of being a superintendent — one who directs the assemblage of causal factors — and agency characterized by possessing direct knowledge of the material cause and the rest, the desire to act, and exertion. Therefore, in the earlier [passage], agency was stated as possessing direct knowledge of the material cause and the rest, desire to act, and exertion; here, agency in the form of superintendence is asserted — and one should note that there is no occasion for the objection of inconsistency raised by the opponent. The intended meaning here is also this: since agency of this kind over earth and the rest is impossible in <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) — who are not omniscient and omnipotent — and is possible only in <s>Īśvara</s> (God), who is eternally all-seeing and all-capable, the inference is not subject to the defect of <s>siddhasādhana</s> (proving what is already established). 'Nor does one who accepts both' — this will be stated in the subsequent text. In the middle [section], he removes the fallacy of <s>anaikāntya</s> (inconclusiveness) incidentally:
'In the seed'

children.text: ' ti / yatra yatra kārye na dṛṣṭaḥ kartā, tatatsarvamipa kāryaṃ prakṛte pakṣīkṛtam / pakṣe ca vyabhicāraśaṅkā na doṣāya, anyathānumānakathāyā eva vilopaprasaṅgāditi bhāvaḥ / '
children.translated_text: — thus. Wherever in any effect a maker is not seen, all such effects are included in the present <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-locus). And the suspicion of deviation in the thesis-locus is not a defect, for otherwise there would be the absurd consequence of the destruction of all inferential reasoning — this is the purport.
'By this'

children.text:
' ti / pakṣāntarbhūtatvenaivetyarthaḥ / ādipadena jñānādi grahyam / na hi svasukhajñānādyarthapravṛttimān jīvastadopakaraṇopādānādṛṣṭasvātmasākṣātkartā / tat upādānādi sākṣātkartṛpūrvakatvarūpasādhyabhāvavati sukhajñānādau
kāryatvasya sattvādvyabhicāra ityapi sukhāderapi pakṣāntarbhāvata eva nirastamityarthaḥ / tatrāpyupādānādisākṣātkartṛpūrvakatvamīśvareṇaiva nirūhyate 'smābhiriti hṛdayam / nanu tarhi jīvasya svasukhādau kartṛtvaṃ na syāditi vācyam / sukhādisampādanārthatassādhanadarśanopādānapravṛttimattvādevopapatteḥ, kulālāderiva dṛṣṭopakaraṇādidarśanopādānādinā ghaṭādau / adṛṣṭakāraṇādhiṣṭhānaṃ tu sarvatra kārye paramātmana eveti dhyeyam / nanvevamapi svajñānādyarthapravṛttipūrvakāle niyamena svasya sākṣātkārābhāvāt svajñānādyupādānabhūtasvātmasākṣātkartṛtvaṃ tadā tasya nāstīti cet, na, ātmanaḥ
svaprakāśatvanayena tadā svātmasākṣātkārasyāpi saṃmānayitavyatvāt / svajñānādau svasya kartṛtvasya svasmṛtimātreṇāpi abhyupagantavyatvādvā na doṣaḥ / upādānādisākṣātkartṛpūrvakatvamiti niyamastu īśvareṇaiva tatra tatra nirvāhyeti ca na vismartavyama / tadarthameva sukhādyapi pakṣīkṛtamiti bodhyam / vyabhicāraṃ parihṛtya siddhasādhanatāṃ pariharati '
children.translated_text: — thus. The meaning is: precisely because they are included within the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-locus). By the word 'ādi' (and so forth), knowledge and the like are to be understood. For the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), who acts for the sake of its own pleasure, knowledge, and the like, is not the direct perceiver of the material cause, instruments, <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit), and its own self for those [purposes]. Therefore, the objection that there is deviation of effectness in pleasure, knowledge, and the like — which lack the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), namely being preceded by a maker who directly perceives the material cause and the rest — is also refuted precisely by including pleasure and the rest within the <s>pakṣa</s>. The heart of the matter is: even there, being preceded by a direct perceiver of the material cause and the rest is accomplished by <s>Īśvara</s> alone. Now, if [one objects that] then the <s>jīva</s>'s agency over its own pleasure and the like would not be possible — [the reply is:] this is not so, because it is explained by the <s>jīva</s>'s possessing activity preceded by the seeing and taking up of perceived instruments for the purpose of obtaining pleasure and the like — just as a potter [has agency] over pots through seeing and taking up perceived instruments and the like. But the supervision of unseen causes is everywhere the function of the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) alone — this should be borne in mind. Now, even so, if [one objects that] since prior to the activity directed at one's own knowledge and the like there is invariably no direct perception of oneself, the <s>jīva</s>'s agency as direct perceiver of its own self — which is the material cause of its own knowledge and the like — does not exist at that time; [the reply is:] no, because by the principle of the self-luminosity of the <s>ātman</s> (self), direct perception of one's own self must be acknowledged even then. Or, there is no defect because the <s>jīva</s>'s agency over its own knowledge and the like may be accepted even through mere self-recollection. But the rule that [effects must be] preceded by a direct perceiver of the material cause and the rest is fulfilled everywhere by <s>Īśvara</s> alone — this must not be forgotten. It should be understood that pleasure and the like are also included in the <s>pakṣa</s> for this very purpose. Having resolved the deviation, he resolves the <s>siddhasādhana</s> (proving what is already established):
'Nor does one who accepts both'

— thus. The meaning is: the postulation of superintendence conducive to the activity of atoms, <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit), and the rest [is not established through <s>jīvas</s>]. He states the reason for its being unjustified [for <s>jīvas</s>]:
'Of those'

children.text: ' miti / draṣṭumeva tadaśaktānāntadadhiṣṭhānakathā keti bhāvaḥ / nanvīśvarasyāpi adhiṣṭhānasāmarthamadṛṣṭaṃ kathaṃ kalpate ? tatrāha '
children.translated_text: — thus. The purport is: what talk of supervision by those who are unable even to perceive them? Now, how is <s>Īśvara</s>'s capacity for supervision established through <s>adṛṣṭa</s>? To that he replies:
'Nor is it so'

children.text: ' iti / adṛṣṭamapi na dṛṣṭavirodhīti bhāvaḥ / kuto na dṛṣṭavirodhaḥ ? atrāha '
children.translated_text: — thus. The purport is: <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit) also does not contradict what is perceived. Why is there no contradiction with perception? To that he replies:
'By another means of knowledge'

children.text: ' iti / atra 'tadasiddhe' riti pāṭhaḥ syādveti sandihyate / pratyakṣādineśvarasyāsiddherasāmarthyasya tasminnadṛṣṭatvādityarthaḥ / nanvanenaivānumānena tasyāsāmarthyaṃ setsyatītyatrāha '
children.translated_text: — thus. Here, one may doubt whether the reading should be '<s>tadasiddhe</s>' (when that is not established). The meaning is: since <s>Īśvara</s>'s incapacity is not established by perception and the like, because it is not perceived in Him. Now, [if one says] that His incapacity will be established by this very inference, to that he replies:
'When it is established as stated'

children.text: ' ti / 'tatsiddhe' riti pāṭhe tu śaktimadīśvarasyaiva vilakṣaṇapramāṇena siddherityarthaḥ / kintat ? tadāha '
children.translated_text: — thus. On the reading '<s>tatsiddhe</s>' (when that is established), the meaning is: because <s>Īśvara</s> who possesses power is established by a distinct means of valid knowledge. What then? To that he says:
'When it is established as stated'
— thus. The word 'sidhyat' (being established) should be connected with the subsequent word
'<s>hi</s>' (for)
— thus is the construal.
'In what is naturally established'

children.text: ' ti / sarvasyārthasya kriyākārakaphalavargāntaḥ pātitayā sarvādhiṣṭhānaṃ tadarthaṃ sarvasākṣātkaraṇamapīśvarasya prāpte / te cākaraṇakatvānnitye eveti bhāvaḥ / '
children.translated_text: — thus. Since every entity falls within the class of action, causal factors, and results, <s>Īśvara</s>'s supervision of all and direct perception of all for that purpose follows. And since those [direct perception and supervision] do not involve instrumental activity, they are eternal — this is the purport.
'Of effectness'

children.text:
' ti / yatra kāryatvaṃ tatra tatra samarthakartṛjanyatvamiti vyāpterityarthaḥ /
kulāladeḥ kiñcidviṣayājñānāśaktī api vidyete / tadalpajñālpaśaktikartī vyāptiḥ kāryatvasya gṛhyate bhūyaḥsahacāradarśanabalāt / tadabhimataviparītāpādakatvādviruddhatvāmiti śaṅkāṃ '
children.translated_text:
— thus. The meaning is: by the invariable concomitance that wherever there is effectness, there is origination by a capable maker.
Even in a potter and the like, there exists ignorance and incapacity with respect to certain objects. [If one objects that] the concomitance of effectness is grasped with a maker of limited knowledge and limited capacity, based on observation of predominant co-occurrence, and [that this] would establish the opposite of what is intended, hence constituting the fallacy of <s>viruddha</s> (contradiction) — this objection
'As for what'
— and so forth, he restates and then resolves:
'Tha'

children.text: ' diti / aprayojakatvāt-kāryakaraṇopayuktatvābhāvātkiñcidviṣayājñānādeḥ / ayaṃ bhāvaḥ-yenākareṇa kartuḥ kāraṇatvaṃ tadrūpāvacchinnakartṛpūrvakatvenaiva kāryatvasya ghaṭādau vyāptirgṛhītā / kiñcidviṣayājñānādimattvena ca na ghaṭādau kāraṇatvaṃ kulālādeḥ / kintu tadupādānādisākṣātkārādhiṣṭhānakṣamatvaviśiṣṭatvenaiva / anyaviṣaye jñānājñāne śaktyaśaktī vā aprayojake prakṛtakāryotpāde / tatsamarthakartṛkatvenaiva vyāptiḥ kāryatvasya / yathā dhūmasyādraindhanasaṃyogaviśiṣṭavahnitvāvacchinnennaiva saṃbandhaniyamaḥ, na tu raktatvakārīṣatvādyanupayuktadharmāvacchinnena, tadvaditi / aprayojakatvamevopapādayati '
children.translated_text: — t. Because of being non-contributory — because ignorance regarding certain objects and the like has no relevance to the production of the effect [in question]. The purport is this: the concomitance of effectness in pots and the like is grasped as being preceded by a maker delimited precisely by that aspect by which the maker has causality. And the potter's causality over pots is not through possessing ignorance regarding certain objects, but precisely through being qualified by the capacity to directly perceive and supervise their material cause and the rest. Ignorance or knowledge regarding other objects, or capacity or incapacity [regarding other things], are non-contributory to the production of the effect in question. Therefore, the concomitance of effectness is with having a capable maker only. Just as the invariable relation of smoke is delimited only by fire qualified by contact with moist fuel, and not by non-contributory properties such as redness or being made of cow-dung — so too is this case. He further establishes the non-contributory character [of partial ignorance]:
'For not'
— thus. 'Ignorance' means ignorance of other objects such as instruments [not involved in the effect in question].
'One's own'

children.text:
' ti / svakāraṇatvenānumīyamānasya
kartuḥsvaniṣpattyupayogisāmarthyādyevākṣipyate kāryatvasya masarthakartṛkatvavyāpteriti kevalavyarirekasya-kevalasya pūrvavartimātrasyānupayogino vyatirekasya-arthāntaragocaraśaktyādyabhāvasya prakṛtakārye prayojakatayāsiddherityarthaḥ / arthāntaraviṣayaśaktyādyabhāvasya vyatireke prakṛtakāryasya vyatireka iti vyatirekasahacārasyāsiddheriti vār'thaḥ / mūlapāṭho 'trānyathā syādvā / tāvataiva-svaniṣpādanopayogijñānaśaktita eva / arthāntaro viṣayo yasyeti bahutrīhiḥ / anyapadārtho jñānādirarthasiddhaḥ / tasya pratiyogitayābhāve 'nvayaḥ / sambandhinaḥ-kāryaniyatapūrvavartinaḥ / akiñcitkarasya-prakṛtakāryānupayoginaḥ / anyathāsiddhasyeti yāvat / atha vikalpamukhenārthāntaraviṣayakājñānādeḥ niyatapūrvavṛttitvamapi pratikṣipati '
children.translated_text: and so forth. The maker, who is being inferred as its cause, has the capacity useful for his own production and so forth drawn in by the effect-nature's pervasion with having a capable maker. The meaning is: the mere negative concomitance alone — the mere prior occurrence [of ignorance] which is unserviceable, i.e., the absence of power and so forth pertaining to other objects — is not established as having a causal role in the effect under discussion. Alternatively, the meaning is: the negative concomitance in the form of 'when there is absence of power and so forth regarding other objects, there is absence of the effect under discussion' — that co-occurrence of the negative concomitance is not established. The root reading here may be different. 'By that much alone' — from the knowledge and power useful for one's own production alone. 'Arthāntaraviṣaya' ('pertaining to another object') is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> (possessive compound). The other term — knowledge and so forth — is established by the matter itself. Its absence is in the role of the counter-correlate. 'Sambandhinaḥ' — that which invariably precedes the effect. 'Akiñcitkarasya' — that which is of no use for the effect under discussion, i.e., that which is established as otherwise accounted for (<s>anyathāsiddha</s>). Now, through a disjunctive method, he also rejects the invariable prior occurrence of ignorance regarding objects other [than the effect under discussion], beginning with
'Moreover'
and so forth. 'Pervading' — that which invariably precedes the effect.
'Not indeed'

children.text: ' prakṛtakāryātiriktasakalakāryopayogijñānasāmarthyavirahaḥ kartari kutrāpyasiddha eveti bhāvaḥ / nanu prakṛtakāryātiriktakatipayaviṣayājñānādi karturiṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ cetyatrāha '
children.translated_text: — the purport is that the absence of knowledge and capacity useful for all effects other than the effect under discussion is never established in any maker.
'Now if'

children.text: ' ti / arthāntarayatkiñcidajñānādi na vyavasthitam / yathā kaścitpaṭakāraḥ ghaṭaṃ na jānāti kaścittu jānāti, kaścittvanyanna jānāti anyastu tajjānātīti prakṛtakarturanyānyaviṣayaṃ jñānamajñānaṃ cāvyavasthitaṃ dṛśyate / paṭādyajñānaṃ ghaṭādyajñānaṃ vā niyataṃ karturdurvacamiti tattadajñānasya tatra tatrānaikāntyānna hetutvamiti bhāvaḥ / sarvasyāpi kartuḥ kiñcidvastu niyamena na jñāyate iti tu durvacamevetyāha '
children.translated_text: and so forth. Ignorance of any arbitrary other object is not fixed. Just as some cloth-maker does not know a pot but another does, and one does not know something else but another knows it — thus the knowledge and ignorance of the relevant maker regarding this or that other object is observed to be unfixed. Since the ignorance of cloth and the like, or the ignorance of pots and the like, cannot be definitively stated of a maker, there is no probative force of that particular ignorance in that particular case, due to inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntya</s>). This is the purport. He states that it is indeed impossible to say that no maker at all definitely fails to know something, beginning with
'Nor is there'

children.text:
' ti / nanu svaviśiṣṭajñānābhāvatvenājñānasya hetutvamupeyate / svapadaṃ prakṛtakāryaparam / vaiśiṣṭyaṃ ca jñāne svaniṣṭhaviṣayatvānirūpakatvasvānya niṣṭhaviṣayatānirūpakatvobhayasambandhena / tathā ca tattadajñānasya tatra tatra vyabhicāre 'pi niruktarūpāvacchinnajñānābhāvasya niyatapūrvavṛttitvasambhava eveti cet, evamapi pūrvokmanyathāsiddhatvaṃ durvārameveti dhyeyam /
kāryatvasyājñātvādiviruddhākārākṣepakatvaṃ kṣityādikartari parihṛtametāvatā /
atha śarīratvalakṣaṇaviparītākārākṣepakatvaṃ pariharati '
children.translated_text: and so forth. Objection: it is accepted that ignorance in the form of the absence of a specific kind of knowledge is the reason. The word 'sva' ('own') refers to the effect under discussion. And the specificity in knowledge is [determined by] the twofold relation of not being a determiner of the object belonging to oneself and not being a determiner of the object belonging to one other than oneself. Accordingly, even though there is deviation of this or that ignorance in this or that case, the invariable prior occurrence of the absence of knowledge delimited in the stated manner is indeed possible — if so, [the reply is:] even so, the otherwise-accounted-for nature (<s>anyathāsiddhatva</s>) stated earlier is unavoidable. This should be noted. Having thus resolved that the effect-nature reason draws in the contradictory qualification of ignorance and so forth regarding the maker of earth and so forth, he now resolves the drawing in of the contradictory qualification of embodiment, beginning with
'Not so'

children.text:
' ti / kartuḥ śarīravattvameveti na niyamaḥ / ekaṃ dehaṃ parityajya dehāntaraparigrahaṇaṃ kurvato jīvasya tadā/ḍaśarīritvādita bhāvaḥ / yogino yogabalājjīvato dehāntaragrahaṇaṃ kurvato jīvasya tadāśarīritvāditi bhāvaḥ / yogino yogabalājjīvato dehāntaragrahaṇaṃ saśarīrasyaiva dṛṣṭamityayogina ityuktam / nanu ayogino 'pi sūkṣmaśarīravata eva sthūladehāntaragrahaṇaṃ
pretyeti na vyabhicāra ityatrāha '
children.translated_text: and so forth. There is no rule that the maker must be embodied. The purport is: when the <s>jīva</s> (individual self), having abandoned one body, takes up another body, it is at that [transitional] moment disembodied. For a <s>yogin</s> (adept), the taking up of another body while alive through the power of <s>yoga</s> has been observed even while embodied — hence [the text] says 'of a non-yogin.' Objection: Even a non-yogin, having only a subtle body, takes up another gross body after death — so there is no deviation [from the rule of embodiment]. To this he responds:
'The previous'

children.text:
' / nanu śrutibalādbhūtasūkṣmaiḥ pariṣvaktasyaiva jīvasya gatyādireṣṭavyā / tānyevendriyaprāṇasaṃsṛṣṭāni sūkṣmadeha ucyate / tathā ca kartuḥ śarīratvaniyame na vyabhicāra iti cet ; atra brūmaḥ / evamapi sthūlaśarīravattvaniyame 'naikāntyaṃ sthitameva / sūkṣmasya tu na mukhyaṃ śarīratvam / amukhyaṃ ca tadīśvaraṃ prati paramāṇūnāmapyakṣuṇṇameva / tathāhi nyāyācāryodayanaḥ paramāṇūnāmīśvara śarīratvamuśatīti /
evaṃ śarīropādāne kartṛtvaṃ jīvasyā śarīrasyaiveti samarthya śarīrapreraṇe kartṛtvamapyaśarīrasyaivetyāha '
children.translated_text: and so forth. Objection: On the strength of scripture, the going and so forth of the <s>jīva</s> enveloped by subtle elements must be accepted. Those [subtle elements] combined with the senses and vital breaths are called the subtle body. Accordingly, there is no deviation from the rule that the maker must be embodied. To this we say: Even so, the inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntya</s>) regarding the rule of possessing a gross body stands. And the subtle [body] does not have embodiment in the primary sense. And non-primary embodiment with respect to <s>Īśvara</s> remains fully intact even for atoms. For indeed, the Nyāya master <s>Udayana</s> accepts that the atoms are <s>Īśvara's</s> body. Having thus established that agency in the taking up of a material cause belongs to the <s>jīva</s> even when disembodied, he also states that agency in the directing of the body belongs to one who is disembodied, beginning with
'Moreover'

children.text: ' ti / adhitiṣṭhataḥ-pravartayataḥ adhiṣṭhātṛdehānupraveśaḥ adhiṣṭhātṛtāvacchedakaghaṭakatā / śarīramadhitiṣṭhato 'dhiṣṭhātṛtāvacchedakaṃ saṅkalpādireva, na tu taccharīramapi / adhiṣṭhānakarmībhūtasya kāṣṭhāde stacchettṛtāvacchedakatvaṃ yathā na tadvaditi bhāvaḥ / nanu svādhiṣṭhātṛsambaddhasya dehasya kathaṃ nādhiṣṭhātṛtāvacchedakatā ? iti śaṅkate '
children.translated_text: and so forth. 'Of one who governs' — of one who directs. The entry [of the governor] into the governed body is the delimiting factor of governorship. For one governing the body, the delimiting factor of governorship is volition (<s>saṅkalpa</s>) and the like alone, not that body itself — just as the delimiting factor of the cutter-nature of a log and the like, which has become the object of governance, is not that [log] itself. This is the purport. Objection: how is it that the body, which is connected with its own governor, is not the delimiting factor of governorship? He raises this objection:
'Of one to be governed'
and so forth. He resolves it:
'Let there be one'

children.text: ' ti / 'ekatattve' ti prācīnamudritapāṭho na saṃśuddhaḥ / 'ekatastvasaṃbaddhasye' ti vānyathā vā pāṭhaḥ saṃbhāvyate / atyantato 'sambaddhasyādhiṣṭheyena tadadhiṣṭhātṛtvasya kāṣṭhāsaṃbaddhasya kuṭhārasya cchettṛtvasyevāsaṃbhavādadhiṣṭheyasambandhinādhiṣṭhātrā bhavitavyamityeva niyamaḥ, na tu dehasaṃbandhinā bhāvyamitīti bhāvaḥ / preraṇaṃ prati preryasambandha eva hetuḥ na dehasambandha ityatra niyāmakaṃ pṛcchati '
children.translated_text: and so forth. The earlier printed reading 'ekatattve' is not correct. The reading is conjectured to be 'ekatastvasaṃbaddhasya' or otherwise. Since for one completely unconnected with the object to be governed, its governorship would be impossible — just as the cutter-nature of an axe unconnected with a log [would be impossible] — there is indeed the rule that the governor must be connected with the object to be governed, but not [the rule] that it must be connected with a body. This is the purport. Since the connection with the object to be directed is the reason for directing, not the connection with a body — he asks for the determining factor in this, beginning with
'Whence'
and so forth. He replies:
'Because'

children.text:
' iti / adhiṣṭhīyamānaṃ-pravartyamānam / svasaṃbandhinā-preryasaṃyoginā / hastādi viśeṣyamatra / ayamāśayaḥ-śarīriṇa eva pravartakatvamiti na niyamaḥ / hastāderapi mānadaṇḍādipravartakatvāt / preryasaṃbandhina eva prerakatvamiti ta saṃbhavati, hastāderapi preryasambandhāditi /
śaṅkate '
children.translated_text: and so forth. 'Being governed' — being directed. 'By one connected with oneself' — by one conjoined with the object to be directed. The hand and so forth is the qualificand here. The intent is: there is no rule that only an embodied being can be a director, since the hand and so forth also directs measuring rods and the like. And it is possible that only one connected with the object to be directed can be a director, since the hand too has connection with the object to be directed. He raises an objection:
'Now if'

children.text: ' ti / pravartanaṃ nāma paravyāpāraprayojakaprayatnavattvam / tacca puruṣasyaiva / sa ca svahastavyāpāreṇa mānadaṇḍādi pravartayati / tathā ca dehatadavayavabhinnavastupravartane dehahastādivyāpārāpekṣāsyeveti neśvarasyānākṛteḥ paramāṇvādyadhiṣṭhātṛtvaṃ saṃbhavatītyāśayaḥ śaṅkituḥ / imamapi niyamamanaikāntyenaiva dūṣayati '
children.translated_text: and so forth. Directing means possessing an effort that causes another's activity. And that belongs to a person alone. And he directs the measuring rod and the like through the activity of his own hand. Accordingly, in the directing of an object other than the body and its parts, there is a dependence on the activity of the body, hand, and so forth — therefore the governorship of <s>Īśvara</s>, who has no body, over atoms and the like is not possible. This is the intent of the objector. He refutes even this rule through inconclusiveness alone:
'That too is not'

children.text:
' ti / saṅkalpagaruḍadhyānādimānasavyāpāramātreṇa hastādivyāpāraṃ vināpi paraśarīrasthaviṣanivartanādidarśanāddehatadavayavavyatiriktādhiṣṭhāne dehādivyāpārāpekṣāniyamo nāstītyarthaḥ / preryasaṃbandho 'pyatra prerakasya jñānadvāraka eveti ca bodhyam / punaḥ śaṅkate
'
children.translated_text: and so forth. Since we observe through mere mental activity — such as volition, meditation on <s>Garuḍa</s>, and so forth — the neutralization of poison located in another's body even without the activity of the hand and so forth, there is no rule that in governing something other than the body and its parts, there must be dependence on the activity of the body and so forth. This is the meaning. And it should be understood that even here, the connection of the director with the object to be directed is through the medium of knowledge. He raises another objection:
'How'

children.text: ' iti / janyajñānādau dehasya hetutvāditi bhāvaḥ / antarnihitottara ākṣipati '
children.translated_text: and so forth. The purport is: because the body is a cause of produced cognition and so forth. He raises [the objection] containing the answer within it:
'What'

children.text: ' miti / dehasya kiṃ saṅkalpe kartṛtvam ? yena yena tadabhāve saṅkalpo na ghaṭetetyarthaḥ / śaṅkate '
children.translated_text: and so forth. What role does the body have in volition, such that in its absence volition would not be possible? This is the meaning. He raises an objection:
'The instrument'

children.text: ' miti / tatra karaṇaṃ śarīramiti cenna, manasa eva karaṇatvādityarthaḥ / tathā ca śarīrābhāve 'pi svahetoreva saṅkalpo bhaviṣyatīti bhāvaḥ / nanu manasaḥ karaṇatve 'pi janyajñānādau dehasyāpyastyevāpekṣāvacchedakatayeti cedatra brūmaḥ-baddhajñānādāveva dehāpekṣā, nānyatra / '
children.translated_text: and so forth. To 'the instrument is the body' — [the reply is] no, because the mind alone is the instrument. This is the meaning. Accordingly, even in the absence of a body, volition will arise from its own cause alone. This is the purport. Objection: Even if the mind is the instrument, the body too has a role as a delimiting factor in produced cognition and so forth. To this we say: The dependence on the body pertains only to bound cognition, not elsewhere.

children.text: manasaivaitān kāmān paśyan ramateya ete brahmaloke
children.translated_text: 'By the mind alone, seeing these desires, he rejoices — these are in the world of <s>Brahman</s>'
'By the mind alone, the creation of the world'

children.text: '-mityādinā muktasyeśvarasya ca manovattvaṃ, tata eva jñānasaṅkalpādikaṃ ca pratīyate / taddehavigame 'pi manaso nityendriyatvopagamādeva śarīrānapekṣasaṅkalpādyupapattiriti / īśvare nityajñānacikīrṣāprayatnavādināṃ tārkikāṇāṃ mate tu na tarāṃ śarīrādyapekṣā / atra manovattvāgantukasaṅkalpādisamarthanaṃ tu tadekadeśimatena vā siddhāntacchāyayā veti bodhyam / manovattve 'niṣṭaprasaṅgaṃ śaṅkate '
children.translated_text: — by such [scriptural passages], the possession of mind by the liberated [soul] and by <s>Īśvara</s> is understood, and from that alone, [the existence of] cognition, volition, and so forth [is established]. Accordingly, even upon the departure of the body, since the mind is accepted as an eternal sense faculty, volition and so forth without dependence on a body are fully justified. According to the view of the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> (logicians) who hold that <s>Īśvara</s> possesses eternal knowledge, desire, and effort, there is even less dependence on a body and the like. Here, the establishing of the possession of mind and adventitious volition and so forth should be understood as either according to a particular school or in accordance with the doctrinal position. He raises the objection of an undesirable consequence from the possession of mind:
'But then in that case'
and so forth. The meaning is: since the possession of mind is pervaded by embodiment and so forth, embodiment and so forth would apply to <s>Īśvara</s>. He resolves:
'Not so'

children.text: ' iti / samarthakartṛpūrvakatvena kāryatvasya vyāptergṛhītatvāt tataḥ kṣityādau sidhyataḥ karturīśvarasyāśarīritvaiśvaryādyeva setsyati '
children.translated_text: and so forth. Since the pervasion of effect-nature with being preceded by a capable maker has been grasped, therefore regarding earth and so forth, what will be established for the maker, <s>Īśvara</s>, is precisely disembodiment, lordship, and so forth.
'An offering suitable to the <s>Yakṣa</s>'

children.text: ' riti nyāyāt / śarīritvādyupagame cāsāmarthyaprasaṅgāt / yathācaitattathā 'nacāsmadāde' -rityanantaravākye vakṣyate / tathā ceśvare śarīratvānaiśvaryādyāpādanaṃ dharmigrāhakamānabādhitamityarthaḥ / draḍhimnaiva-dṛḍhatayaiva / 'samarthakartṛkatvārthadraḍhimnaive'ti samastapāṭhaḥ sādhīyān / manasaḥ śarīritvādivyāpyatvamapi nirākaroti '
children.translated_text: — by this reasoning. And if embodiment and so forth were accepted [for the creator], there would be the consequence of incapacity. How this is so will be stated in the subsequent sentence beginning '<s>na ca asmad ādeḥ</s>' (not from one such as us). And thus, the imposition of embodiment, non-sovereignty, and so forth upon <s>Īśvara</s> (God) is not established because it is not contradicted by a valid means of knowledge that apprehends the property-bearer — this is the meaning. <s>Draḍhimnā</s> means 'with firmness' — that is, with strength. The compound reading '<s>samarthakartṛkatvārthadraḍhimnaiva</s>' (by the very firmness of the meaning of having a competent maker) is preferable. He also refutes the pervadedness of <s>manas</s> (mind) by embodiment and so forth —
'<s>manasaḥ</s>' (of the mind) —

children.text:
' iti / sarīrābhāve 'pi prāyaṇāvāntaralayādau nityendriyatayā manasaḥ sattvātkālāvacchedena śarīravyāpyatvaṃ manaso nāstītyarthaḥ / nanvevamapi saśarīrasyaiva kartṛtvaṃ tatra tatra dṛṣṭāmiti
śarīrikartṛkatvena vyāptiḥ kāryatvasya kuto na gṛhyata ityatrāha '
children.translated_text: — thus. Even in the absence of a body, since <s>manas</s> (mind) exists as an eternal sense organ during death, intermediate dissolution, and so forth, <s>manas</s> does not possess pervadedness by body in the sense of being temporally delimited — this is the meaning. But even so, if it is objected that agency is observed everywhere only of an embodied being, and therefore why should the <s>vyāpti</s> (invariable concomitance) of <s>kāryatva</s> (effect-nature) with embodied agency not be grasped? — to this he says:
'<s>yāvad dhī</s>' (as far as cognition) —

children.text: ' ti / dṛṣṭānuguṇaṃ kāryānugumatvena dṛṣṭamata eva vyāptyupayogi thadrūpaṃ tadavacchinnenaiva vyāptireṣṭavyā / jñānaśaktyoreva ca kāryānugumatā / te yadyapi karmaparavaśe kulālādau śarīrādhīne ; naitāvatā śarīrādervyāpakatāvacchedakakoṭiniveśa iti bhāvaḥ / evamanabhimatāpadakatvaṃ parihṛtam / athābhimataviśeṣasiddhiprakāraṃ prapañcayati '
children.translated_text: — thus. The form that is useful for establishing <s>vyāpti</s> (invariable concomitance), being conducive to the effect in accordance with what is observed, the <s>vyāpti</s> should be accepted as delimited only by that form. And it is only <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) and <s>śakti</s> (capacity) that are conducive to the effect. Although these are dependent on <s>karma</s> and subordinate to the body in the case of a potter and such, that alone does not place embodiment and the like in the class of delimiters of the pervader — this is the purport. Thus the objection of entailing unintended consequences has been resolved. Now he elaborates the manner of establishing the desired specific attributes —
'<s>na ca asmad ādeḥ</s>' (not from one such as us) —

children.text:
' riti / aparyantavistārasya anavadhikāyāmavato 'paricchinnasya prādeśikaśarīrakaḥ parimitadeśavartiparicchinnamūrtimān / alaṃ-samarthaḥ / śiṣṭaṃ spaṣṭam /
śaṅkate '
children.translated_text: — thus. One of unlimited extent, of immeasurable dimension, unlimited — [cannot be created by] one having a local body, one of limited spatial presence and finite form. <s>Alam</s> means 'capable.' The rest is clear. The opponent raises a doubt —
'<s>īdṛśena</s>' (by one of such nature) —

children.text: ' ti / akarmavaśyatvāśarīritvasarvajñatvādiviśiṣṭakartrā kāryatvasyāvinābhāvo ghaṭādau na dṛṣṭa iti śaṅkiturbhāvaḥ / sāmānyadharmāvacchinnavyāptigrahādeva pakṣadharmatābalasahakārātpakṣīyasādhya viśeṣasiddhiriti hārdena pratibandīmāha '
children.translated_text: — thus. The purport of the objector is that the invariable co-presence of <s>kāryatva</s> (effect-nature) with a maker possessing the specific attributes of not being subject to <s>karma</s>, being disembodied, being omniscient, and so forth, is not observed in a pot and such things. Since the <s>vyāpti</s> (invariable concomitance) is grasped as delimited by general properties alone, the establishment of the particular <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved) in the <s>pakṣa</s> (subject) follows from the strength of the property-possession in the subject with the assistance of that — with this essential idea he states the counter-objection:
'<s>atigahane</s>' (in what is very profound) —
— thus. He has the refutation spoken through the mouth of the objector himself —
'<s>yādṛśaḥ</s>' (of which kind) —

— thus. <s>Yādṛśaḥ</s> means of such a form as having extremely dense, ground-touching, continuous, and ever-extending streams [of smoke]. <s>Tādṛśaḥ</s> means a great fire [of corresponding magnitude].
'<s>tat</s>' (that) —
— thus. Meaning: capable of producing the aforementioned type of great smoke. Here —
'<s>tādṛśa-tat-saṃpādana-samarthaḥ</s>' (capable of producing that of such a kind) —
— this may be the compound reading. He states the parallel with the subsequent [argument] —
'<s>tad idam</s>' (this here) —

children.text: ' iti / yathā deśakālaparimāṇādiviśeṣo vahneranaikāntyāddhūmavyāpakatāvacchedakaghaṭako na bhavati, kintvādrendhanayugvahnitvamātraṃ tathā, evaṃ manuṣyatvādi sahacaritamipi na kartṛtāvacchedakakoṭighaṭakam / anyatrāpi kartṛtvadarśanāt / kintu sāmarthyamātraṃ tathetyāha '
children.translated_text: — thus. Just as specific features of location, time, magnitude, and so forth of fire do not constitute components of the delimiting condition of the pervader-status of smoke — rather, only fire-nature as such, together with fuel and the like, is sufficient — so too, humanity and other co-occurring attributes are not components of the class of delimiters of agency. Because agency is observed elsewhere too. Rather, mere capacity alone is sufficient — so he says:
'<s>yathaiva</s>' (just as) —

children.text:
' ti / dhūmātparvate vahniviśeṣānumānāt kāryatvāt kṣityādau kartṛviśeṣānumānasya na vailakṣaṇyam / yathā tatrābhimataviśeṣasiddhistathā prakṛte 'pīte bhāvaḥ /
atha sapakṣadarśanamātreṇa sarvadharmāpādane pratibandī vivakṣurāha '
children.translated_text: — thus. There is no dissimilarity between the inference of a specific fire on a mountain from smoke and the inference of a specific maker of earth and so forth from <s>kāryatva</s> (effect-nature). Just as in that case the desired specific attributes are established, so too in the present case — this is the purport. Now, intending to state a counter-objection that mere observation in the positive instance would entail attribution of all properties, he says:
'<s>api ca</s>' (moreover) —
