children.text: ' ti / vibhudravyasaṃyogina ityanenāvibhutvaṃ manaso vivakṣitam / vibhudvayasaṃyogasya tārkikairanupagamāt / jñānādyasamavāyikāraṇasaṃyogāśrayatayā manaḥsiddhirita jñānetyādiviśeṣaṇam / ātmamanaḥsaṃyogasyaiva hi jñānādāvasamavāyihetutvaṃ tanmatam / jñānāyaugapadyācca tasyāṇutvaṃ matam, niḥsparśatvaṃ ca / sparśavattve bhūtatvaprasaṅgāt / bhūtatve cābhūtaviśeṣaguṇagrahakatvāsaṃbhavāt / atrāyaṃ pratitarko vivakṣitaḥ-mano yadi paricchinnaparimāmavat syāt kriyāvadvā tarhi sparśavadbhavediti / bhūyaḥ sahacāradṛṣṭasyāpi kvacidvyabhicāra ityasyedamekaṃ nidarśanam / atha nidarśanamanyatpradarśayati '
children.translated_text: — thus. By the phrase 'being conjoined with a non-ubiquitous substance,' the non-ubiquity of <s>manas</s> (mind) is intended, since the <s>Tārkikas</s> (logicians) do not accept conjunction of two ubiquitous substances. Since <s>manas</s> is established as the locus of conjunction that is the non-inherent cause of <s>jñāna</s> (cognition) and so forth, hence the qualifier 'of cognition' and so on. For their doctrine is that the conjunction of <s>ātman</s> (self) and <s>manas</s> alone is the non-inherent cause of cognition and such. And from the non-simultaneity of cognitions, its atomic nature is held, as well as its being devoid of <s>sparśa</s> (touch). Because if it possessed touch, it would be an element. And if it were an element, it could not grasp the specific qualities of non-elements. The intended counter-argument (<s>pratitarka</s>) here is this: if <s>manas</s> were of limited magnitude or possessed of motion, then it would possess touch. This is one illustration of the principle that even what is observed as frequently co-occurring may occasionally deviate. Now he presents another illustration —
'<s>kathaṃ ca</s>' (and how) —

children.text: ' ti / aniyatādhiṣṭhāneti padanchedaḥ / yadyapi mahato vāyorgatiśīlasyāniyatādhiṣṭhānatvamudbhūtasparśavattvāt spārśanapratyakṣatvaṃ ca bhūyo dṛṣṭam / athāpi vāyavīyatvenānumitasya dehavyāpinastvagindriyasya niyatādhiṣṭhānatvamaspārśanatvaṃ cābhimatam / atra pratitarkaḥ-tvaco vāyavīyamahatkāryatve udbhūtasparśavattvādi bhavediti / nidarśanāntaraṃ '
children.translated_text: — thus. The word-division is '<s>aniyata-adhiṣṭhānā</s>' (having an undelimited substrate). Although it is frequently observed that <s>vāyu</s> (wind), being great, having a mobile nature, and having an undelimited substrate, possesses manifest touch and is perceptible through tactile sensation; nevertheless, the skin-organ, which is inferred as being of the nature of <s>vāyu</s> and pervades the body, is held to have a delimited substrate and to be imperceptible by touch. Here the counter-argument is: if the skin were a great product of <s>vāyu</s>, it should possess manifest touch and so forth. Another illustration —
'<s>taijasasya</s>' (of what is fiery) —

children.text:
' ti / kāryatejaso mahimaguṇavato rūpasparśayorudbhūtatvaṃ jvalanādau / sparśamātrasyodbhūtatvaṃ bharjjitakapālavahnyādau / rūpamātrasyodbhūtatvaṃ prabhādau / evaṃ rūpasparśaubhayatadanyatarodbhavasya bhūyo dṛṣṭatve 'pi cakṣuṣo rūpadiṣu rūpādiṣu
rūpamātravyañjakatvenānumitataijasabhāvasya tadubhayānudbhavaḥ kathamityarthaḥ / cakṣuṣaḥ taijasamahatkaryatve rūpasparśānyatarodbhavaḥ syāditi prasaṅgo 'tra bodhyaḥ / pratitarkāṇāmābhāsatvamityāśayena prativakti paraḥ '
children.translated_text: — thus. In the case of produced <s>tejas</s> (fire/light) possessing the quality of greatness, both <s>rūpa</s> (color/form) and <s>sparśa</s> (touch) are manifest — as in flame. Touch alone is manifest in heated potsherds, fire, and the like. Color alone is manifest in radiance and the like. Thus, although the manifestation of color, touch, both, or neither is frequently observed, how is it that the eye, whose fiery nature is inferred through its capacity to reveal color alone among color and other [qualities], lacks the manifestation of both? — this is the meaning. The implied objection to be understood here is: if the eye were a great fiery product, it should manifest either color, touch, or one of the two. Intending that the counter-arguments are merely specious, the opponent replies —
'<s>atha</s>' (now then) —

children.text: 'ti / tattadviśeṣāṇām-udbhūtarūpasparśānyataraspārśanatvasparśavattvādīnāṃ bhūyaḥ / sahacāradarśanamātreṇa cakṣurādāvāpād.mānānāṃ yogyānupalambhabādhitatvamiti nāpādakavyāpakatvamāpādyasyeti bhāvaḥ / yadyapi manaso 'ṇutvāttatra sparśavattvasya yogyānupalambhabādho durvacaḥ / tathāpi tatra tadupagame 'nekaniyamabhaṅgaprasaṅgostyeva / tadāha '
children.translated_text: — thus. Those specific properties — manifestation of color or touch or either, perceptibility or imperceptibility by touch, possession of touch, and so forth — are merely observed in frequent co-occurrence, and when applied to the eye and such, they are contradicted by non-apprehension of a fit object; therefore there is no pervader-pervaded relationship between what produces and what is produced — this is the purport. Although in the case of <s>manas</s>, given its atomic nature, it is difficult to assert contradiction by non-apprehension of fitness for its possessing touch, nevertheless, if that were accepted, there would be the consequence of breaking many established rules. That he states —
'<s>tad abhyupagame</s>' (if that is accepted) —

children.text: ' iti / yathā- manasaḥ sparśavattve bhūtatvaprasaṅgaḥ / bhūtatvānupagame sparśavato bhūtatvameveti niyamabhaṅga/ bhūtatvopagame cendriyāntaravadabhūtātmaviśeṣaguṇāgrāhaktavāttiḥ / tadgrāhakatvopagame cābhūtaviśeṣaguṇāgrāhakatvaniyamasyāpi bhaṅga / iti / evaṃ cakṣurādāvapi udbhūtarūpavattvādisvīkāre nānāniyamabhaṅgaprasaṅgo 'nusandheyaḥ / vipakṣe bādhakaviraheṇāpādyāpādakayorvyāpyavyāpakabhāvāsiddhiḥ / tathā ca pratitarkāṇāṃ chinnamūlatvaṃ ca vivakṣitam / '
children.translated_text: — thus. For example: if <s>manas</s> possessed touch, there would be the consequence of its being an element. If elementhood is not accepted, then the rule that whatever possesses touch is an element would be broken. If elementhood is accepted, then like other sense organs it would be unable to grasp the specific qualities of non-elemental <s>ātman</s> (self). If that grasping capacity is accepted, then the rule that non-elemental specific qualities cannot be grasped [by elements] would also be broken. Thus also in the case of the eye and so forth, if manifestation of color and such were accepted, the consequence of breaking many rules should be considered. In the counter-instance, through the absence of a defeater, the pervaded-pervader relationship between what is to be attributed and what attributes remains unestablished. And thus the intended point is that the counter-arguments are uprooted.
'<s>tathā abhyupagame</s>' (given such acceptance) —

children.text: ' iti mana-prabhṛterniḥsparśatvādyabhyupagama ityarthaḥ / tulyanayena kratṛtve saśarīratvamiti niyamo 'pi nāstītyāśayavānāheśvaravādī '
children.translated_text: — meaning: given the acceptance of touchlessness and so forth of <s>manas</s> and other [sense organs]. With the same reasoning, the <s>Īśvaravādin</s> (theist) says, intending that the rule 'agency requires embodiment' also does not hold —
'<s>hanta tarhi</s>' (well then!) —

children.text:
' ti / svasmin prasañjitapratitarkanirākaramayukteḥ paramukhenaivānuvācanajanitaharṣadyotako 'yaṃ / hantaśabdaḥ / saśarīratve śarīradvāropalambhaprasaṅga īśvarasya / kramavattve cāsārvajñyādiprasaṅgaḥ / prakṛtaṣṭadharmavattvāt sārvajñyādyugamaśca na saṃbhavati / sādhānānuṣṭhānarāhityātprakṛṣṭadharmasyānupapatteḥ / īśvarasya sa dharmo nitya evopeyata iti pakṣe ca dharmasāmānyasya vihitakriyājanyatvaniyamabhaṅgaḥ / akarmatve ceśvarasya saśarīratvāyogaḥ / taccharīrasya nityatvopagame ca sāvayavatvasya kāryatvavyāpyatvaniyamabhaṅgaḥ / tathā ca kṣityāderapi kāryatvāsiddhestatkartṛtveneśvarānumānāyoga iti bahuramūhanīyam /
sahacāramātreṇa kartṛtvasya na saśarīratvādivyāptiḥ, vipakṣe bādhakavirahāditi ca hārdam /
nanu cakṣurādestaijasādibhāve 'pi tattadviśeṣasya pramāṇasiddhatvānna tadviruddhāpādānasambhavaḥ / naivaṃ tvīśvarīyaviśeṣāṇāṃ mānasiddhatvamiti cettatrāha '
children.translated_text: — thus. This word '<s>hanta</s>' expresses the delight generated by having the refutation of the counter-argument raised against oneself stated through the opponent's own mouth. If <s>Īśvara</s> (God) were embodied, there would be the consequence of perception through the body. If [His cognition were] sequential, there would be the consequence of non-omniscience and so forth. And the attainment of omniscience and such through possession of the relevant <s>dharma</s> (merit) is not possible, because extraordinary <s>dharma</s> cannot arise without the performance of <s>sādhana</s> (prescribed practice). And if it is held that God's <s>dharma</s> is eternally present, then the rule that <s>dharma</s> in general is produced by enjoined action would be broken. If God is not subject to <s>karma</s>, embodiment would be impossible for Him. And if His body is accepted as eternal, then the rule that being composite is pervaded by being an effect would be broken. And thus, since <s>kāryatva</s> (effect-nature) of earth and such would itself be unestablished, inference of <s>Īśvara</s> as their maker would be impossible — much here is to be reflected upon. The essential point is that mere co-occurrence does not establish the <s>vyāpti</s> (invariable concomitance) of agency with embodiment and so forth, due to the absence of a defeater in the counter-instance. But if it is objected that in the case of the eye and such, the specific attributes of being fiery and so on are established by <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge), so attribution of what contradicts them is impossible, whereas the specific attributes of God are not similarly established by <s>pramāṇa</s> — to that he says:
'<s>dṛśyante</s>' (they are seen) —

children.text: ' iti / nītayaḥ-nyāyāḥ, anumānāni / īśvare 'pyabhimataviśeṣeṣu santi pramāṇānītyarthaḥ tānyeva prapañcayati '
children.translated_text: — thus. <s>Nītayaḥ</s> means reasonings, that is, inferences. The meaning is: there exist <s>pramāṇas</s> (valid means of knowledge) for the desired specific attributes of <s>Īśvara</s> (God) as well. He elaborates those very [reasonings] —
'<s>yathā</s>' (just as) —

children.text:
' iti / 'tathe' ti pāṭhe tu tathā hi nītayo dṛśyanta ityanvayaḥ / tathā-īśvarīyābhimataviśeṣasādhakāḥ / īśvarasya sraṣṭṛtve tādanumānamuktaṃ pūrvam / tasya
pravartayitṛtve tadāha '
children.translated_text: — thus. In the reading '<s>tathā</s>' (so), the syntactic connection is: 'so indeed reasonings are seen.' <s>Tathā</s> means: those that establish the desired specific attributes of <s>Īśvara</s>. The inference for God's being a creator has been stated earlier. Regarding His being the activator, he says —
'<s>paramāṇv-ādi</s>' (atoms and so forth) —

children.text: ' ti / vivādāspadamiti pakṣatāsambhavadyotakaṃ viśeṣaṇam / sādhyatadabhāvānyataranirṇaye hi pakṣatātivartate / sādhyatadabāvavattvavipratipattiviṣayībhūtamiti /tadarthaḥ / sādhyavattvena sandihyamānamiti phalitam / sādhyasandehasya pakṣatātvaṃ prācāṃ matam / siddhisthale 'pyāhāryasaṃśayādevānumitsayā bhavatyanumānamiti bodhyam / preraṇaṃ ca paraprṛttyanuguṇasaṅkalpaprayannavattvalakṣaṇam / paramāṇvādigocarāvīśvarasya saṅkalpaprayatnau prasādhya sākṣātkāramapi tādṛśaṃ sādhayati '
children.translated_text: — thus. 'The entity in dispute' — this qualifier serves to indicate the status of being a thesis (<s>pakṣatā</s>). For when either the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) or its absence is determined, the thesis-status lapses. [Meaning:] it is the object of disagreement regarding whether it possesses the probandum or not — this is the meaning. The result is: it is doubted as to whether it possesses the probandum. The thesis-status [being constituted by] doubt regarding the probandum is the view of the ancients. It should be understood that even in established cases, inference functions through deliberately assumed doubt and the desire to infer. And 'directing' (<s>preraṇa</s>) is characterized by possessing volition and effort conforming to the activity of another. Having established <s>Īśvara's</s> volition and effort regarding atoms and the like, he also establishes direct perception of that nature:
'Just so'

children.text: ' ti / tadvadeva-kandukādipravṛttivadeva / kandukādipravṛttāvupādānaṃ kandukādi, upakaraṇaṃ daṇḍādi / tatsākṣātkārī daṇḍena kandukādi pravartayati / tataśca tatra pravṛttirūtpadyate / evaṃ paramāṇvādipravṛtterjñānādyarthāntarātmapravṛtterapyupādānopakaraṇaparamāṇvādyadṛṣṭādisākṣātkartātra sādhyate / na caitatsākṣātkartṛtvaṃ jīvānāmiti na taiḥ siddhasādhanam / atīndriyārthānāmapi sākṣātkāraḥ phalito 'trānumāne /
children.translated_text: — thus. 'Just like that' means: just like the functioning of a ball and the like. In the functioning of a ball and the like, the material cause is the ball and the like; the instrument is the stick and so forth. One who directly perceives that [material cause] sets the ball and the like in motion with a stick. And thereupon motion arises in it. Similarly, the direct perceiver of the material cause, instruments, atoms, <s>adṛṣṭa</s> and the like — whether through knowledge and so forth, or through an activity that is of the nature of something else — is what is to be proved here, regarding the functioning of atoms and the like. And this direct perception does not belong to <s>jīvas</s>; therefore it is not already-established by them. In this inference, direct perception even of supersensible objects is the result.

body.translated_text: Objection: Let 'being an effect' be [established] by the stated reasons. But how does that [alone] lead to having a maker? Since there is no evidence that the maker is a cause of effects in general, and since the origination of earth and the like is possible from other causes alone without a maker — to this he says:

children.translated_text: 'Perceptible'

children.text: ' iti / tat-paramāṇvādi / atīndriyārthasākṣātkartā kaścit saṃbhavatītyatraiva tātparyamevaṃvadhānumānapratipādakānāṃ paramācāryāṇām / kṣityādikarturabhimata ekatve prayogamāha '
children.translated_text: — thus. 'That' means atoms and the like. The true intent of the supreme teachers (<s>paramācāryas</s>) who propound such inferences is precisely this: that there exists someone who directly perceives supersensible objects. He states the formal proof regarding the intended oneness of the maker of earth and the like:
'Conforming to one will'

children.text: ' ti / idamacetanaprapañcajātam, acaitanyātam, acaitanyāt acetanatvāt, ekecchānuvidhāyi ekacetanasaṅkalpanusāri / atrānvayyudāharaṇaṃ svadehaḥ // 16 //
children.translated_text: — thus. This entire assemblage of non-conscious manifold, because of being non-conscious (<s>acaitanya</s>), conforms to a single will — follows the volition of a single conscious being. The corroborating instance by positive concomitance here is one's own body. // 16 //

body.translated_text: Now, directly making supersensible objects the thesis, he proves their perceptibility:
All conscious beings, presided over by one, perform their effects,
because their capacity for action depends on the connection with a body — like the skin and other [sense organs]. // 17 //
The world, which is the seat of this dispute, has one chief person (<s>pradhānapuruṣa</s>),
because it consists of the conscious and the non-conscious — like a country with one king. // 18 //

Thus [ends] the <s>Īśvarasiddhi</s> (Proof of God's Existence) in the <s>Siddhi-traya</s> (Triad of Proofs), graciously composed by the supreme teacher, the venerable <s>Bhagavad Yāmuna Muni</s>, the foremost champion in establishing the <s>Viśiṣṭādvaita</s> (Qualified Non-dualism) doctrine.

children.translated_text: 'By one'
— thus. 'Like skin and the like' means: like the sense organs such as skin and the like. // 17 //

body.translated_text: Having established that the functioning of the non-conscious manifold conforms to the will of <s>Īśvara</s>, he also establishes the same for the conscious manifold:

children.translated_text: 'One'

children.text: ' ti / ekaḥ pradhānapuruṣo yasya tadekapradhānapuruṣam / ekapradhānapuruṣaviśiṣṭamityarthaḥ / puruṣasyaikasya prādhānyaṃ niyantṛtvasvāmitvalakṣaṇam / vaiśiṣṭyaṃ niyāmyatvaśeṣatvādinā // 18 //
children.translated_text: — thus. 'That which has one chief person' — this means: qualified by having one chief person — this is the meaning. The supremacy of one person, characterized by being the controller and master. The qualification [of the world] is through being controlled, being subordinate, and so forth. // 18 //

body.translated_text: He states the inference that proves the specific nature of being the lord and master of the entire world:

children.translated_text: (Commentary)

children.text: niṣprayojanatvātkartṛtvāmīśvarasya na saṃbhavatītyāderapi parāso 'tra vibhāvyaḥ / yathā-jīvarakṣārthameva tāvavadīśvarasya jagadvyāpāraḥ / nanu tarhi sukhottarameva jagat sṛjet / maivam / jīvīyakarmāpekṣayā tathā tathā sarjanāt / nanu karmāpekṣitve 'naivaśvaryaṃ tasya prasajyeta / na / aparādhānuguṇadaṇḍadharasyeva rājñaḥ tattatkarmaphalaniṣpādakasyeśvarasyāpi aiśvaryātiśayasyaiva prasiddheḥ / adṛṣṭādīnāmadhiṣṭhātṛtvādi hi tasya mahate vaibhavāya / yathākarma phalapradatvāt svāmitvamapi sarvasya tasmin pratitiṣṭhatyeva / sarvapradhānatvādṛṣṭādhiṣṭhātṛtvādisādhanapramāṇopanyāsakānāṃ cācāryacaraṇānāmetaddhārdagra mityunnayāma iti dik //
children.translated_text: The refutation of [the objection] 'creation is impossible for <s>Īśvara</s> due to purposelessness' and the like should also be elaborated here. Thus: <s>Īśvara's</s> engagement with the world is for the protection of the <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) alone. Objection: If so, he should create a world that is nothing but happiness. Not so; because he creates in accordance with the <s>karmas</s> of the <s>jīvas</s>. Objection: If he is dependent on <s>karma</s>, his sovereignty would be diminished. No; because, just as for a king who administers punishment in accordance with offenses, for <s>Īśvara</s> too, who brings about the fruits of the respective <s>karmas</s>, it is precisely a surplus of sovereignty that is well-established. For his superintendence over <s>adṛṣṭa</s> and the like is [a sign] of his great glory. Because he bestows fruits in accordance with <s>karma</s>, his mastership over all is also well-established. Since [the text demonstrates] that <s>Īśvara</s> is supreme over all and is the superintendent of <s>adṛṣṭa</s>, we conclude that this was the heart of the matter for the revered teachers who present the evidence for these proofs — this is the indication.

body.translated_text: The remaining portion of the text is not found anywhere beyond this [point].
This straightforward commentary has been composed by me on what has been obtained [of the text].

children.translated_text: the son-jewel of the illustrious teacher known as <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇamācārya</s>,

one who has mastered the four <s>Tantrīs</s> to their furthest shore, whose fame rests in all directions, the embodiment of compassion, descended in the divine lineage of the illustrious author of the <s>Śrī Bhāṣya</s>, a connoisseur residing in <s>Śrībhūtapura</s>, the emperor among scholars,
the illustrious <s>Āsūri Rāmānujācārya</s>,

a servant of the <s>Śrī Vaiṣṇavas</s>, who has mastered the heart of the systems of word-meaning, sentence-meaning, and valid means of knowledge through devoted service at the lotus feet of the lord of preceptors, by
<s>Aṇṇaṅgācārya</s>,
who is learned in <s>Nyāya</s>, <s>Vyākaraṇa</s>, the crown-jewel [of logic], and both <s>Vedāntas</s> — this commentary on the <s>Īśvarasiddhi</s>, composed [by him],
[is called] <s>Siddhāñjana</s> (The Collyrium of Established Truth) —
may it be supremely victorious!
